tax_assumptions._ignore_note: Kilian 2026-09-28: ignore taxes for now (he has money set aside for the liability). Set false to use the tax facts below.
tax_assumptions._future_note: Combined rate you'd expect on today's embedded gains when you'd otherwise sell (15% federal + ~6% state once working). Drives the sell cost and the gain-harvest suggestion.
tax_assumptions._tax_note: Kilian 2026-09-28: taxable account; ~$20,000 internship wages in 2026 plus realized gains; claimed as a dependent by a parent living in CA; full-time student under 24 living in CT. Assumed (not confirmed): domicile stays CA (a student living away at school keeps the parents' domicile, FTB Pub 1031), CT dorm is not a permanent place of abode so CT does not tax investment income; kiddie tax applies (earned income not more than half of his support). Federal 2026 figures from IRS Rev. Proc. 2025-32; CA brackets are 2025 (FTB Tax News Oct 2025), 2026's not published yet.
tax_assumptions._other_unearned_note: Dividends etc. this year (rough: GOOGL + META dividends). Counts toward the kiddie-tax threshold.
tax_assumptions._kiddie_note: Unearned income above $2,700 (2 x $1,350, Rev. Proc. 2025-32) is taxed at the parent's rate, federal (Form 8615) and CA (FTB 3800). Applies to a full-time student 19-23 whose earned income is not more than half of his own support.
tax_assumptions._parent_note: Kilian 2026-10-20 22:04Z: parent in NYC, 37% federal bracket. Parent's NY/NYC rates do not apply to Kilian's gains (no NY kiddie tax under Form 8615).
tax_assumptions._flat_note: Kilian 2026-10-20 22:04Z: the parent claiming him lives in New York City (37% federal bracket; NY 9.65%, NYC 3.876% at the parent's income). Federal kiddie tax (Form 8615): unearned income above kiddie_threshold ($2,700) at the parent's federal rates, short-term 37%, long-term 20% (the 37% bracket is above the 20% LTCG start, Rev. Proc. 2025-32); up to the threshold at Kilian's own federal rates, 10% short-term (wages $20k less the $16,100 dependent standard deduction leave ~$3.9k taxable, inside the 10% band to $12,400) and 0% long-term. New York has no kiddie tax when Form 8615 is used: the child's investment income is reported on the child's own NY return and taxed at the child's own rates (NYS IT-201-I, 'Does your child have investment income over $2,700?'). So NY and NYC tax every gain at Kilian's own marginal rates: NY 5.40% ($13,900-80,650) + NYC 3.762% ($12,000-25,000), single, 2026 schedules (NYS IT-2105-I 2026); NY dependent standard deduction $3,100. Assumed: Kilian is domiciled at the parent's NYC home (a dependent student keeps the parents' domicile) and his CT dorm is not a permanent place of abode. NIIT dropped (Kilian 2026-10-21 00:48Z 'yes you may drop it'; it was kept per his 2026-10-01 20:32Z ask): Form 8960 applies it on the child's own MAGI over $200,000 (single), which his income does not reach. Short-term = 37% + 9.162% = 46.162%; long-term = 20% + 9.162% = 29.162%; own rates under the threshold 19.162% / 9.162%. Was CA (41.3% / 28.1% / 14% / 2%) until 2026-10-20. Net losses offset gains; up to $3,000 deducts at the own short-term rate. Bracket mode (mode 'brackets') still holds the CA schedule and is not updated.
tax_assumptions._short_term_all_note: Kilian 2026-10-28 card 'Assume short-term on all' (thread 'Fix AMAT target vs sell mismatch'): every holding is assumed sold within the year at the short-term rate, so a trim only pays the same tax H years sooner; band per year = q tau (1 - (1+d)^-H) / H + spread / T. Overrides lot_aware_horizon; false restores it.
tax_assumptions._lot_aware_note: Kilian 2026-10-20 card 'Lot-aware' (Assumption audit thread): a short-term lot's trim band compares selling now with holding it to its one-year date and selling long-term: band per year = q (tau_now - flat_long_term_rate (1+d)^-X) / X, X = years until the oldest (FIFO) lot turns long-term (floor 1 day), plus spread / T. Long-term lots keep the T-year rule (years_until_you_would_otherwise_sell, future_rate_on_deferred_gains, Claude defaults 2026-09-28). false restores the T-year rule for every lot.

agents.method_text: Blend of 19x FY28 (Nov-27 to Oct-28) non-GAAP EPS $24.19 = $459.5 (65%) and a DCF of FY28 FCF/share $20.32 at 11% (10y 5.31% + 5.7pt), 3% terminal = $334.9 (35%): 0.65 x 459.5 + 0.35 x 334.9 = $415.9 -> $416 for Oct-2027. FY28 EPS assumes AI revenue $180B (management line of sight $230B), FY27 AI ~$115B per guidance.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: FY28 EPS $24.19 x 19x. FY28 revenue $235.2B = AI $180B + non-AI semis $18.25B + software $36.92B; op income $144.6B (semis 57.5%, software 83%); net interest -$2.42B; tax 16%; 4.94B shares

inputs_detail.derivation: Hock Tan, Q3 FY26 call: 'In 2027 we have secured the supply to again double AI revenue to approximately $115 billion' (raised from 'in excess of $100 billion' on the Q2 call [10]).

Management: 'line of sight for fiscal 2028 AI semiconductor revenue growth to again double to $230 billion. Here again, we have secured the supply' [6], but Tan also said they judged the GW count 'conservatively' because shells/power limit how many of ~30 GW reach production. Anchors: (a) purchase commitments rise from $52,674M (FY27) to $72,952M (FY28), +38.5% [4]; scaling the $115B FY27 guide by that ratio gives 115 x 72,952/52,674 = $159B, a floor because later-year commitments are still filling in; (b) house capex base 2028 $2,255B [16]: $115B/$1,841B = 6.2% in 2027; $180B = 8.0% of 2028 (+1.8pt share gain, backed by Anthropic +10 GW and OpenAI >5 GW line of sight [6]); $230B would need 10.2%. $180B sits between the commitment floor and management's figure.
Q4 FY26 guide ~$4.3B x 4 = $17.2B, +3%/yr for two years = $18.25B.
Q4 FY26 guide ~$8.7B (Q3 $8,752M, +29% y/y) x 4 = $34.8B, +3%/yr for two years = $36.92B (growth slows as VMware conversion laps).

Q3 semis segment margin 61% [6]; Q4 implied ~60% (66% x $34.8B = $22.97B less software ~84% x $8.7B = $7.31B, leaves $15.66B / $26.1B semis revenue = 60%). XPU memory content and rack mix dilute a further ~2.5pt as AI rises to ~77% of revenue.
Q3 software operating margin ~84% [6]; trimmed 1pt.
198.25 x 0.575 + 36.92 x 0.83 = 113.99 + 30.64 = $144.64B; check: segment sum reproduced Q3 (61% x 20.84 + 84% x 8.75 = 20.06 vs reported non-GAAP op income $20,095M [1]).
Q3 non-GAAP interest expense -$703M + other income $98M = -$605M x 4 = -$2.42B; held flat (debt paydown offset by no assumed rise in interest income).
CFO: non-GAAP tax rate for Q4 and FY26 ~16% [6]; Q3 actual 3,118 / (20,095 - 703 + 98) = 16.0% [1].
Q4 FY26 guide ~4.94B non-GAAP diluted shares excluding buybacks [6]; held flat ($10.1B authorization remaining through 2026-12-31 [2] roughly offsets SBC dilution).

(144.64 - 2.42) x (1 - 0.16) / 4.94 = $24.19. Management says it is 'very much on target to exceed $30 in earnings per share in fiscal 2028' [6]; our figure is 19% lower because of the $180B AI haircut and margin dilution.

memo.title: AVGO: long a de-rated AI compounder at ~13.5x FY28 consensus; target $390, research target (12m) $407, stop $261
memo.call_reason: The published 12-month target ($390.49) is above the $349.57 price, conviction is medium, and there is no special situation; the supervisor's 8% cap limits size and the book gets 2 shares.
memo.one_liner: Broadcom has fallen ~30% from its June high while earnings rose ~43%. It trades at ~13.5x LSEG FY28 EPS of $25.86, against management's $115B FY27 / $230B FY28 AI roadmap. We underwrite consensus EPS, not management's >$30, and still get a $407 research target (12m) (+16%) and a $390 target (+12%, P(gain) 60%), with the Q4 print on ~Dec 10 as the first test.

thesis.point: Earnings are compounding faster than the stock is falling: the de-rating is multiple, not fundamentals.
thesis.evidence: Q3 FY26 revenue $29.6B (+86% y/y), AI semis $16.7B (+221%), non-GAAP EPS $3.32, FCF $13.7B. The Q4 guide is $34.8B with $21.7B AI. Yet the stock is back at its end-2025 level with EPS ~43% higher and ~30% below the June high, at ~18x FY27 consensus ($19.38) and ~13.5x FY28 ($25.86).

thesis.point: We do not need management's numbers: consensus EPS at a below-peer multiple gets to ~$407.
thesis.evidence: Management guides $115B FY27 and $230B FY28 AI revenue and >$30 FY28 EPS; LSEG consensus is $25.86. All five agents value on NTM EPS of $24.7-26.5 at 16.5-17x, i.e. at or below consensus. Every $1 of FY28 EPS the market underwrites is worth ~$16-17/share, so each beat on the path toward >$30 is upside to the target.

thesis.point: The XPV financing scare is smaller than the headline: expected loss ~$0.5/share.
thesis.evidence: The 10-Q (Note 10) shows a Backstop of one customer's 5-year lease obligations: 85% of lease balance owed less rack resale value, max ~$29B, fair value not material, nothing paid, plus a facility under which the customer may issue Broadcom up to $42B of convertible notes (none issued). BofA's $370B is a hypothetical 20 GW build-out; its loss case on the existing tranche is ~$2.9B. We deduct ~$2-2.5B (~$0.5/share).

memo.variant_view: The variant view is modest, and it cuts both ways. Against the options market we are more constructive: its implied 12-month median is ~$364 with P(gain) 54%, while our blended target is $390 with P(gain) 60%, because the agents give credit for ~2x EPS growth at a compressed ~16-17x NTM multiple that the market is not paying for today. Against the sell side we are far more cautious: 38 analysts rate it Strong Buy with a median target of $525.5 (mean $517), which in effect capitalizes management's >$30 FY28 EPS at ~18-20x. We underwrite LSEG's $25.86 and a discount for six-customer concentration, Google's move toward MediaTek and the XPV overhang. So this is not a contrarian call. It is a 'consensus earnings, de-rated multiple' call that is roughly half-way between options pricing and the Street.

valuation.methods: The research target (12m) of $407 is the mean of five independent agents ($391-425), valued as of Sep 2027. Legs: (1) P/E on NTM (mostly FY28) EPS of $24.7-26.5 at 16.5-17x = $420-439 (40-60% weight); (2) FCF yield of 5-5.5% on ~$97-122B NTM/FY28 FCF = $388-441; (3) DCF at 10% WACC, 3% terminal growth = $311-373 (agents 1 and 5); (4) SOTP with AI at 16x after-tax earnings = $333-388 (agents 2 and 3). EV-based legs deduct $35.4B net debt ($59.419B debt less $23.975B cash) and ~$2-2.5B expected XPV loss; all use 4.94B non-GAAP diluted shares. $407 is ~16x NTM EPS of ~$25.5, dividends (~$2.60/yr) excluded. The published $390.49 target is the median of the blended distribution (67% options market, 33% agents after calibration), below the research target (12m) because of the 44-58% volatility and the fat left tail. Expected value is $435; quartiles $291 / $522.

BKNG room nights grew 6.0% YTD 2026 (1,008M vs 951M) against arrivals of ~+1-2%, a spread of ~4.5 pts, helped by domestic travel (CFO Steenbergen, src 3: domestic high single digits, international mid single digits). Q4 FY2026 +2.5% y/y (292.1M): October disruptions (Middle East, European unrest; CFO, src 3) and the toughest comp of the year; the company guide is 1-3% (src 2) and Q3 beat the top of its guide (CFO, src 3), so I sit just above the midpoint, not at the top. FY2027 +5% in Q1-Q3 (arrivals assumed +3%, the bottom of UN Tourism's January 2026 3-4% range as the conflict fades, plus a spread narrowed to ~2 pts for rising AI/meta-search and alternative-accommodation competition) and +7% in Q4 FY2027 against the depressed Q4 FY2026 base; FY2028 +5% (arrivals +3%, spread +2). Alternatives: (a) hold the YTD 2026 spread of 4.5 pts on +3% arrivals = +7.5%/yr (upside); (b) UN Tourism's 2026 forecast +1.5% plus spread 2 = +3.5%; (c) consensus revenue FY2027 $31.5B (src 9) implies ~+8% revenue, consistent with ~5% room nights. agents.reasoning: Primary-document build. The Q3 2026 10-Q, release and transcript give actuals (room nights 345M +7%, gross bookings $54.5B +10%, adjusted revenue $9.79B, take rate -15 bp) and the Q4 guide (room nights 1-3%, adjusted revenue 0-2%, EBITDA about flat). The $900M FTC revenue reduction plus a $100M accrual is booked as a one-off and an equity adjustment. The record: annual first revenue guides were beaten in FY2024 (+3.4% vs mid) and FY2025 (+8.0%), but FY2026's first guide (low double digits) is now a ~3% miss, so I give no beat premium. Drivers: room nights from global travel demand (UN Tourism 2026 cut to +1-2%) plus a share-gain spread narrowed from ~4.5 pts to ~2 for AI and competition; ADR +3% (CFO); take rate down 10 bp/yr on flights mix; marketing flat as a share of GB; non-marketing opex +6.6% net of the $650M transformation run-rate. FY2027 revenue is $31.4B (consensus $31.5B, StockAnalysis 2026-11-13) and EPS ~$11.7 (consensus adjusted $12.23, ~4% below). Buybacks of ~$9B/yr cut shares 6.5%/yr. Valuation: P/E on horizon NTM EPS, exit 14.6x from the k = 0.8 shrink of 13.1x toward the 22.5x two-peer median, giving a research target (12m) of $184.82 (+17%). The downside (P10, $123) and upside (P90, $243) move room nights, take rate and marketing and ±3 turns of multiple; the left tail is fatter, consistent with 39% realized volatility. The room-night spread is the biggest judgment call (±7-10%), flagged for Kilian. Research was limited: numeric Q2/Q3 2026 quarter guides and a 2027 UN Tourism forecast were not found, and the SEC refused direct curl (filings read via WebFetch and the cached companyfacts).

memo.title: BKNG: low-conviction Long sized for portfolio fit. Trough multiple and buybacks against an unresolved AI-agent overhang
memo.call_reason: Low-conviction, portfolio-fit Long. The target ($179.61) is above the $163.31 price, but the supervisor rated sizing conviction low (0.52), below the medium minimum. The owner took it anyway on 2026-10-01 as a deliberate exception, replacing Microchip, because it lifted the book's forward Sharpe the most (0.594 to 0.66) and correlates only about 0.10 with AVGO.
memo.one_liner: Booking trades at about 13.7x NTM consensus, at its 2022 trough, while buybacks shrink the share count 6-8% a year. That supports a $179.61 12-month target and a $194 research target (12m). The stock-specific edge is thin (an idiosyncratic de-rating has beaten SPY only half the time), so this is a capped 6-share position held mainly because it diversifies a book otherwise driven by AI semis and power.

thesis.point: 1. The valuation already prices a lot of damage.
thesis.evidence: At $163.31 BKNG is about 13.7x NTM consensus (FY2027 EPS $12.37, 33 analysts, flat over 90 days). The supervisor rebuilt realized-forward P/E history: the ex-COVID median is about 19x, with troughs of about 15x (2011-12), 16.7x (2018) and 11.3-13.8x (2022). The FCF yield is about 7.8% on LTM FCF of $9.54B. A flat multiple plus EPS growth alone gets to about $180 by Sep 2027.

thesis.point: 2. Buybacks turn mid-single-digit volume growth into mid-teens EPS growth.
thesis.evidence: There were 751.4M shares on Jul 27, 2026. About 22M were retired in Q2, and $14.5B of authorization remains, so the count shrinks 6-8% a year. Q2 FCF was $3.6B (+16% y/y). FY2026 consensus EPS of $10.45 is +14.6% on FY2025's split-adjusted $9.12.

thesis.point: 3. The AI-agent fear is running ahead of the numbers.
thesis.evidence: The CEO says AI-generated traffic is 'significantly below 1%' of room nights. In Q2 room nights grew +5% and marketing was 4.7% of gross bookings, with no sign yet of lost share or rising marketing intensity. Booking is a hotel partner in Google's agentic AI Mode and has an ad deal with OpenAI. The Sep 23 sell-off came from Expedia's Meta Muse deal, which is a headline and not a number in Booking's results.

memo.variant_view: There is no real variant view against the Street, and our target is below it. Our $179.61 target sits under every one of the 35 analyst targets (weighted median $234.34, low $188), because we do not assume the market closes the AI discount within 12 months: the forecast median ($178-180) is below our own $194 research target (12m). Our view differs mainly from the options market. The options-only distribution centres at $165.64 with P(gain) 0.513, against our blended P(gain) of 0.591 and expected value of $190.51. The research adds roughly 8pp of upside probability from the trough multiple and the buyback math. That gap is modest and the supervisor treats it as thin edge, so the case for owning BKNG here rests as much on what it does for the book as on beating consensus.

valuation.methods: Supervisor's reconciled research target (12m) is $194 (agents $187-198, mean $194.4). It blends two methods. P/E (weight 0.6): NTM EPS at Sep 2027 of about $13.3 (FY2027 consensus $12.37 less 2%, FY2028 about +12.5-13%) x 14.5x = $193. FCF yield (weight 0.4): FY2027 FCF of about $10.45B over about 700M average diluted shares = about $14.9 per share at a 7.6% yield = $196. It then deducts about $1-2 for expected legal costs. The 12-month target is $179.61, the median of the blended distribution, which puts 0.67 weight on the options market and 0.33 on research. The expected value is $190.51 and P(gain) is 0.591.

trade.entry: Supervisor plan: two tranches. Buy 3 shares now near $163 and 3 after the Q3 2026 print (most likely Nov 3-5), provided the print does not show the AI tell (marketing above 4.7% of gross bookings with room nights below guidance).
trade.exit_or_add: Exit on a close below $120, the thesis break: about 9.7x FY2027 EPS, which needs a fundamental break. Also exit if the Q3 or Q4 print shows marketing intensity rising with room nights of 0-2%. Exit or swap if a re-solve shows the Sharpe lift is gone, for example if a medium-conviction name now adds more to the book or BKNG's correlation to holdings rises, because portfolio fit is the main reason we own it. Take profit at $232.69, near the Street median. Do not add beyond 6 shares while conviction is low and the 10% cap binds. Adding needs conviction raised to medium, for example after a Booking agent-distribution deal or a clean Q3 print with stable marketing intensity.

what_changes_our_mind: Q3 2026 (about Nov 3-5): marketing above 4.7% of gross bookings together with room nights below the +3-5% guide. That would be the first sign that AI agents are hitting the earnings and not only the multiple. We would exit.

Booking announces an agent-distribution deal with Meta Muse or OpenAI, or discloses agent-driven bookings growing through its own rails. That would remove the 'shut out' fear and would justify raising conviction to medium and completing or adding to the position.

Book re-solve: if BKNG no longer gives the biggest Sharpe lift (for example a medium-conviction candidate beats 0.66, or its correlation to AVGO and the rest of the book rises well above about 0.10), the portfolio-fit reason for this exception is gone and we would rotate out.

tax_assumptions._kiddie_note: Unearned income above $2,700 (2 x $1,350, Rev. Proc. 2025-32) is taxed at the parent's rate, federal (Form 8615) and CA (FTB 3800). Applies to a full-time student 19-23 whose earned income is not more than half of his own support.

tax_assumptions._flat_note: Kilian 2026-10-20 22:04Z: the parent claiming him lives in New York City (37% federal bracket; NY 9.65%, NYC 3.876% at the parent's income). Federal kiddie tax (Form 8615): unearned income above kiddie_threshold ($2,700) at the parent's federal rates, short-term 37%, long-term 20% (the 37% bracket is above the 20% LTCG start, Rev. Proc. 2025-32); up to the threshold at Kilian's own federal rates, 10% short-term (wages $20k less the $16,100 dependent standard deduction leave ~$3.9k taxable, inside the 10% band to $12,400) and 0% long-term. New York has no kiddie tax when Form 8615 is used: the child's investment income is reported on the child's own NY return and taxed at the child's own rates (NYS IT-201-I, 'Does your child have investment income over $2,700?'). So NY and NYC tax every gain at Kilian's own marginal rates: NY 5.40% ($13,900-80,650) + NYC 3.762% ($12,000-25,000), single, 2026 schedules (NYS IT-2105-I 2026); NY dependent standard deduction $3,100. Assumed: Kilian is domiciled at the parent's NYC home (a dependent student keeps the parents' domicile) and his CT dorm is not a permanent place of abode. NIIT dropped (Kilian 2026-10-21 00:48Z 'yes you may drop it'; it was kept per his 2026-10-01 20:32Z ask): Form 8960 applies it on the child's own MAGI over $200,000 (single), which his income does not reach. Short-term = 37% + 9.162% = 46.162%; long-term = 20% + 9.162% = 29.162%; own rates under the threshold 19.162% / 9.162%. Was CA (41.3% / 28.1% / 14% / 2%) until 2026-10-20. Net losses offset gains; up to $3,000 deducts at the own short-term rate. Bracket mode (mode 'brackets') still holds the CA schedule and is not updated.
tax_assumptions._short_term_all_note: Kilian 2026-10-28 card 'Assume short-term on all' (thread 'Fix AMAT target vs sell mismatch'): every holding is assumed sold within the year at the short-term rate, so a trim only pays the same tax H years sooner; band per year = q tau (1 - (1+d)^-H) / H + spread / T. Overrides lot_aware_horizon; false restores it.
tax_assumptions._lot_aware_note: Kilian 2026-10-20 card 'Lot-aware' (Assumption audit thread): a short-term lot's trim band compares selling now with holding it to its one-year date and selling long-term: band per year = q (tau_now - flat_long_term_rate (1+d)^-X) / X, X = years until the oldest (FIFO) lot turns long-term (floor 1 day), plus spread / T. Long-term lots keep the T-year rule (years_until_you_would_otherwise_sell, future_rate_on_deferred_gains, Claude defaults 2026-09-28). false restores the T-year rule for every lot.

agents.reasoning: Round 1 facts stand: FY26 revenue $1.34B; Q1 FY27 $479M (+115%) at 68% non-GAAP GM; Q2 guided to $525-535M; FY27 >85% (about $2.5B; EPS consensus $6.31); FY28 consensus EPS about $9.63. It also established three things that cut against my round-1 numbers, and I verified them. First, weak cash conversion: Q1 OCF was only $90.2M because inventory rose $62M to $313M. I therefore cut FY28 FCF to $1.25B and Sep-2027 net cash to about $1.8B, which lowers the DCF to $205 and EV/sales to $224. Second, heavier concentration: one direct customer is 43% of revenue. Third, credible Marvell competition on 1.6T AECs, with Mizuho cutting its target on lower peer multiples. Those justified trimming the P/E multiple to 23.5x ($235). The blended fair value falls from $233 to $224, about 6% above the $210.97 close. Scenarios are $110/$228/$350 at 27/48/25, a mean of about $226, with the bear weight raised for concentration and competition. For the ladder I used a lognormal with a median of about $214 (below fair value for execution risk) and a sigma of about 0.68, then trimmed the far right tail as in round 1 so the mean matches the scenarios. That gives P(>=211) of 0.51, P(<127) of 0.23 (slightly fatter than round 1's 0.21), and P(>=422) of 0.10. The analyst average target of about $280 (range $185-350) remains optimistic evidence. memo.title: Dycom: no buy today. Research target (12m) $294.37 says cheap, but the blended 12-month target $231.80 (+4.9%) clears no hurdle; revisit at or under ~$206 or on the late-November Q3 FY27 print
memo.call_reason: The published 12-month target $231.80 is only +4.9% above $221.05, below DY's 12.3% beta-adjusted required return (binding: below_beta_return, so the book buys 0 shares), and rubric conviction is low; the price is above its Entry below level of about $206.42.
memo.one_liner: Kilian's driver build, with the middle trim to the Communications backlog path he chose on 2026-11-02 at 7:26 p.m. ET, values Dycom at a research target (12m) of $294.37 (+33%) on only 13.2x NTM EPS, and insiders bought in September, but the options market (12-month median $208.08, P(gain) 46%) weighs 67% of the published target and sees a carrier-capex slowdown after AT&T's 10-21 capex cut and MasTec's Communications slump. We do not buy today; we buy at or under about $206, or re-underwrite after the late-November Q3 FY27 print shows whether Communications backlog is still growing.

thesis.point: The driver build (approved set plus Kilian's middle backlog trim) gives a research target (12m) of $294.37, +33% from $221.05, on a multiple well below peers.
thesis.evidence: Horizon NTM P/E 13.2x (own 12.13x today vs 18.65x whole-company peer median of MTZ, PWR, PRIM, MYRG) weighted 0.7 ($288.63) and LTM EV/EBITDA 10.2x on pro-forma own EBITDA weighted 0.3 ($307.76); the five independent forecasts, made before the trim, span $299.55-$315.37 (the trim takes -2.7% off the untrimmed $302.46). Build EPS FY27 ~18.3-18.5 vs Zacks 15.98 and StockAnalysis 17.06.

thesis.point: Demand is slowing, not breaking: Communications backlog is flat while carrier capex is trimmed, and BEAD and long-haul land mostly after the 12-month horizon.
thesis.evidence: DY NTM Communications backlog 5,376 (Q1 FY27) -> 5,362 (Q2 FY27), flat; the path now in the set (Kilian's middle trim, 2026-11-02 7:26 p.m. ET) needs 5,420 in Q3 and 5,580 in Q4 (was 5,450 / 5,650), then +1.75% a quarter in FY28 and +1.5% in FY29. AT&T cut 2027-28 capital investment to $22-23B a year from $23-24B but kept >60M fiber locations by 2030; Verizon held 2026 capex at $16-16.5B. MasTec Communications backlog fell 7.5% q/q (flat y/y) with customer deferrals. All 56 BEAD final proposals are approved; >270,000 route miles, ~58% buried, construction 'in earnest' in FY28.

thesis.point: Insiders bought near current levels and the company keeps beating its own guide, which supports the base case through the Q3 print.
thesis.evidence: Open-market purchases: CEO 850 shares at $296.76 (09-09), directors 700 at $286.92 (09-01) and 350 at $280.62 (09-23). Q3 FY27 guide adj. EPS $4.33-4.79; the build carries ~5.2, Street 4.33 (whisper 4.55, 80% range 4.24-4.88), after six straight EPS beats of the guide midpoint.

memo.variant_view: Two consensus views bracket us. Sell-side analysts (11, Strong Buy, median $525, mean $520.91, range $375-625, as of 10-09) are stale, set mostly May-September before the 61% fall from $566.47, and get zero weight in the target. The options market's 12-month distribution is the other pole: median $208.08 (below spot), 15th-85th range $111.42-$312.30, P(gain) 46%, with 1-year implied volatility ~60%. Our research leg (median $268.97, P(gain) 63.5%) is more constructive because the build follows DY's beat record and puts BEAD, long-haul and data-center work into the multiple; the published blend (67% market, 33% research) lands at $231.80. So the variant view is real on value (research target (12m) $294.37 vs options median $208) but not strong enough to clear the hurdle at today's price: the market is pricing a carrier capex slowdown (AT&T's 10-21 cut, MasTec's deferrals) that our path reflects only in part even after the middle trim Kilian chose on the supervisor's recommendation (four of five forecasters and the supervisor had called the original approved path full). Events past the 12-month horizon cut both ways and are weighed through the multiple: FTTH programs mature around 2030-32 (p 0.45, about -$12/sh), BEAD and long-haul extend Communications past the FTTH peak (p 0.5, about +$10/sh), a data-center construction turn in CY2028-29 (p 0.25, about -$10/sh), and carrier consolidation pricing (p 0.3, about -$6/sh); keeping ~29% of DY's discount to peers (exit k=0.8) is how the visible FTTH end date is priced.

tax_assumptions._future_note: Combined rate you'd expect on today's embedded gains when you'd otherwise sell (15% federal + ~6% state once working). Drives the sell cost and the gain-harvest suggestion.
tax_assumptions._tax_note: Kilian 2026-09-28: taxable account; ~$20,000 internship wages in 2026 plus realized gains; claimed as a dependent by a parent living in CA; full-time student under 24 living in CT. Assumed (not confirmed): domicile stays CA (a student living away at school keeps the parents' domicile, FTB Pub 1031), CT dorm is not a permanent place of abode so CT does not tax investment income; kiddie tax applies (earned income not more than half of his support). Federal 2026 figures from IRS Rev. Proc. 2025-32; CA brackets are 2025 (FTB Tax News Oct 2025), 2026's not published yet.
tax_assumptions._other_unearned_note: Dividends etc. this year (rough: GOOGL + META dividends). Counts toward the kiddie-tax threshold.
tax_assumptions._kiddie_note: Unearned income above $2,700 (2 x $1,350, Rev. Proc. 2025-32) is taxed at the parent's rate, federal (Form 8615) and CA (FTB 3800). Applies to a full-time student 19-23 whose earned income is not more than half of his own support.
tax_assumptions._parent_note: Kilian 2026-10-20 22:04Z: parent in NYC, 37% federal bracket. Parent's NY/NYC rates do not apply to Kilian's gains (no NY kiddie tax under Form 8615).
tax_assumptions._flat_note: Kilian 2026-10-20 22:04Z: the parent claiming him lives in New York City (37% federal bracket; NY 9.65%, NYC 3.876% at the parent's income). Federal kiddie tax (Form 8615): unearned income above kiddie_threshold ($2,700) at the parent's federal rates, short-term 37%, long-term 20% (the 37% bracket is above the 20% LTCG start, Rev. Proc. 2025-32); up to the threshold at Kilian's own federal rates, 10% short-term (wages $20k less the $16,100 dependent standard deduction leave ~$3.9k taxable, inside the 10% band to $12,400) and 0% long-term. New York has no kiddie tax when Form 8615 is used: the child's investment income is reported on the child's own NY return and taxed at the child's own rates (NYS IT-201-I, 'Does your child have investment income over $2,700?'). So NY and NYC tax every gain at Kilian's own marginal rates: NY 5.40% ($13,900-80,650) + NYC 3.762% ($12,000-25,000), single, 2026 schedules (NYS IT-2105-I 2026); NY dependent standard deduction $3,100. Assumed: Kilian is domiciled at the parent's NYC home (a dependent student keeps the parents' domicile) and his CT dorm is not a permanent place of abode. NIIT dropped (Kilian 2026-10-21 00:48Z 'yes you may drop it'; it was kept per his 2026-10-01 20:32Z ask): Form 8960 applies it on the child's own MAGI over $200,000 (single), which his income does not reach. Short-term = 37% + 9.162% = 46.162%; long-term = 20% + 9.162% = 29.162%; own rates under the threshold 19.162% / 9.162%. Was CA (41.3% / 28.1% / 14% / 2%) until 2026-10-20. Net losses offset gains; up to $3,000 deducts at the own short-term rate. Bracket mode (mode 'brackets') still holds the CA schedule and is not updated.
tax_assumptions._short_term_all_note: Kilian 2026-10-28 card 'Assume short-term on all' (thread 'Fix AMAT target vs sell mismatch'): every holding is assumed sold within the year at the short-term rate, so a trim only pays the same tax H years sooner; band per year = q tau (1 - (1+d)^-H) / H + spread / T. Overrides lot_aware_horizon; false restores it.
tax_assumptions._lot_aware_note: Kilian 2026-10-20 card 'Lot-aware' (Assumption audit thread): a short-term lot's trim band compares selling now with holding it to its one-year date and selling long-term: band per year = q (tau_now - flat_long_term_rate (1+d)^-X) / X, X = years until the oldest (FIFO) lot turns long-term (floor 1 day), plus spread / T. Long-term lots keep the T-year rule (years_until_you_would_otherwise_sell, future_rate_on_deferred_gains, Claude defaults 2026-09-28). false restores the T-year rule for every lot.

agents.method_text: 60% P/E plus 40% SOTP. The P/E leg is 21x core on CY2028E EPS of $17.0 (= $357), plus about $15/share of after-tax net financial assets, for $372. The SOTP leg is $348. The blend is about $362, against $361 on 2026-10-02.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: At Oct 2027 the market prices CY2028 EPS. Consensus CY2028 EPS is $17.89 (MarketScreener); I trim about 5% for 2027-capex D&A and use $17.0. The core multiple is 21x: inside the 10-peer range of 8.6-33.7x, about 7% above the peer median of 19.6x and below the mega-cap median of 24.4x. That gives $357, plus about $15/share of after-tax net financial assets (cash net of debt, SpaceX, non-marketable book) that consensus EPS does not capture. Total about $372.

$17.89 x 0.95. I haircut about 5% for depreciation on 2027 capex. The standing view's Big-4 base is +47% in 2027 ($733B to $1,080B). Applied to Alphabet's $200B 2026 midpoint, that gives about $295B, which the CFO calls a 'significant' increase. At the call's 60% servers / 40% DC mix, that adds about $35-40B a year of run-rate D&A from 2028. I cannot verify how much of it consensus already carries. Equivalent to +12.6% on the $15.10 CY2027 consensus.

Peer CY2027 P/E: median 19.6x, range 8.6-33.7x across 10 names; mega-cap four median 24.4x. GOOGL today is 23.0x all-in, or (347.68-15)/15.10 = 22.0x core. I take 21x, a modest premium to the median that I argue persists through the horizon. GOOGL's CY2027 EPS growth is +27% against a peer median of +15%. Visibility comes from contract, not forecast: $513.9B of Cloud backlog, just over half recognisable within 24 months (10-Q). Margins are top-quartile (Services 41.8%, Cloud 35.6%). I stay below today's 22x because FCF is negative (Q2 -$5.9B), buybacks are zero (10-Q), and capex rises significantly in 2027. [citation gate 2026-10-06: the 19.6x median rests on S&P Global adjusted (ex-SBC) EPS via Stock Analysis, an aggregator basis inconsistent with GOOGL's GAAP consensus. On MarketScreener EPS checked against 10-K GAAP EPS, at Oct 6 closes, the median of this set's comparable names is 21.7x (META 21.7x, MSFT 24.5x, AMZN 24.4x, ORCL 17.9x, CRM 23.0x, RDDT 21.1x, ADBE 11.1x, NOW 59.6x)]

agents.reasoning: Delta refresh of my 2026-10-02 file. I re-checked filings first. EDGAR shows no 8-K, 10-Q or proxy since Aug 10; the only new filing is an Oct 2 Form 4. So I re-opened and confirmed every reported figure that feeds my fair value at source: the Q2 8-K, the 10-Q, the Q2 call transcript, and the June 5 and Aug 10 8-Ks. The only company releases are the Oct 6 Constellation PPA (890 MW of uprates, 20 years; a separate 2,700 MW, 15-year supply deal; first uprate 2028; cost undisclosed) and the Sep 30/Oct 1 Gemini 4 Argon preview (Fairwind-only, no GA date). Neither changes a 12-month number. Neither does the stock's move: +1.2% Oct 2-6, in line with QQQ's +1.3%. What did change is consensus. CY2027 EPS is now $15.10 (S&P Global; 24/7 Wall St shows $14.47 to $15.10 in 90 days), against $14.84 in my last file. MarketScreener carries CY2028 at $17.89. I also built the 10-peer comp set my prior file lacked, on one CY2027 basis. Its median is 19.6x P/E and 11.9x EV/EBITDA; GOOGL is at 23.0x all-in and 22.0x core. I now apply 21x core, down from 21.5x and anchored to that peer set, to CY2028E EPS of $17.0 (consensus less about 5% for 2027-capex D&A, sized from the standing capex view: Big-4 2027 base +47%), up from $16.5. With about $15/share of stakes, the P/E leg is $372. The SOTP is unchanged at $348. The blend is $362, against $361. The ladder uses median ≈ fair value $362 (+4%), a fat-tailed lognormal mixture (27% sigma at 70%, 40% at 30%, about 31% effective vs 32% realised), and P(≥ spot) of 0.55. The scenario mean is $368 (22/53/25 at $245/$368/$475), consistent with right skew. Thesis break stays $255. For one month, the Q3 print is about 97% inside the window, two-sided, centred at about $349. Lane: 9 of the 15 non-comp sources are primary (60%). The 30 data pages behind the comp table (3 per peer, required by the 2026-10-03 peer rule) are not counted. No option data was used.

agents.reasoning: Skeptic lane. Starting facts (filings): Q2-26 revenue $119.8B (+24%), operating income $40.8B, Cloud $24.8B (+82%) with $8.8B OI, Cloud backlog $513.9B [1][2]. What the consensus may be underweighting: (1) Earnings quality. H1-26 pretax income $216.2B includes $135.9B of equity-security gains (SpaceX IPO and other marks; $94.1B of SpaceX stock, mostly locked up [2][42]) [9][1], so trailing P/E of ~17x is misleading. On ex-gains consensus the stock is 23.2x CY27 [14]. (2) Cash. Q2 FCF -$5.9B, TTM $53.3B [1]. Consensus FCF is $8.4B in 2026 and -$36.7B in 2027 on capex of $201.7B and $301.0B [15], consistent with the standing AI-capex view (Alphabet 2027 consensus $285-357B) [40]. Purchase commitments jumped to $707B [3]. (3) Funding mix. Buybacks went from $13.2B in Q2-25 to zero [1]. Alphabet sold 58M Class A/C shares (net $20.5B) plus $10B to Berkshire, $19B of 6.25% mandatory convertibles, and set up a $40B ATM [4][5][6], plus $45B of bonds in Feb/Aug [7][8][39]. (4) Credit is pricing more risk. On like-for-like tenors, new-issue spreads widened from Feb to Aug: 10y T+63 -> T+85, 40y T+95 -> T+130, despite unchanged AA+/Aa2 ratings [7][8]. The Feb sterling deal included a 2126 century bond at gilts +120bp [41]. That is a mild, not alarming, signal. (5) Concentration and circularity. Anthropic reportedly accounts for over 40% of the backlog [31], and Google backstops financing of Anthropic's TPU purchases [32]. These are press reports (The Information, via Silicon UK), used here only to size bear-case probability, not as valuation inputs. (6) Sentiment is crowded: 0 sells and 4 holds out of 55 analysts; insiders sold ~$8.7M and bought $0 over 3 months [37]. Visible Form 4s are routine 10b5-1 or vesting [11][12][13], so this is not a red flag. Alt-data and markets: StatCounter puts Google at 89.94% of worldwide search in Sep-26 [35]. On Kalshi (via Octagon, Oct 2, week of Oct 5), 'Above 20.5%' Google share of OpenRouter text-model requests traded ~75% and 'Above 19.9%' 97%, with 30,430 contracts on the latter [36]. That reads as a solid but not dominant AI-model position. Privacy litigation remains a recurring cost (shareholder proponents cite a $425.7M privacy jury verdict [38]; PriceRunner $2.1B damages and the $5.2B EU Android payment in Q2-Q3 [3]). What weakens the bear case: the ad tech remedy decision rejected the AdX divestiture and imposed a 6-year behavioral decree [27][28][29][30], removing the largest structural legal tail. The balance sheet remains AA+. Operating momentum is real. Valuation: P/E (21.8x, between the all-peer median 19.8x and the US median 23.5x) on haircut NTM EPS gives $360. EV/EBITDA at the peer median (10.5x) gives $320. Blended fair value is $346, about 0.5% below spot. Scenarios: 257/348/440 at 25/50/25 (mean ~$348). The ladder is a lognormal mixture around those (sigma 0.22/0.17/0.17), giving a log-sd of ~0.27 and median ~$348. This is somewhat tighter than the 32% realized vol, because the realized figure includes the Mar-May 2026 re-rating (weekly close $274 in late March to a $408.61 high in May) [43], and wider than base-rate large-cap moves only in the left tail. Research limits: Twelve Data and Alpha Vantage estimate and statistics endpoints were plan-restricted, so consensus comes from MarketScreener and StockAnalysis. Seeking Alpha, Axios and some trade press were not fetchable.

memo.title: GOOGL: Long, small. 25% core EPS growth at 22x with the Anthropic/SpaceX stakes as a free option; target $371.53 (+8.4%)
memo.call_reason: The published target ($371.53) is above the $342.75 close, P(gain) is 0.59 and sizing conviction is medium, so this is a small, staged long. It is not a special situation.
memo.one_liner: Alphabet trades at about 21x forward core EPS while FY2027 consensus EPS grows about 25% with revisions running 8 up to 1 down, Cloud grows 82% on a $514B backlog, and roughly $13-15/sh of SpaceX/Anthropic stakes carry a November IPO option. The edge is modest (+8% to target against 36% implied vol), so we buy 2 shares in two tranches around the Q3 print and keep the stop at $256.52.

thesis.point: Earnings compound at a multiple that already prices in the capex debate.
thesis.evidence: FY2027 consensus core EPS is about $14.92 (+25%), with 8 upward and 1 downward revision in 30 days. NTM core EPS of about $16.2-16.9 at the horizon, at about 22x, gives $356-372 before stakes. The ~$257B 2027 capex consensus is already in that multiple.

thesis.point: Cloud is now a second profit engine, not an option.
thesis.evidence: Q2 2026 Cloud revenue grew about 82% with a $514B backlog, and TPU system sales to third parties begin in 2027. Backlog conversion is what supports FY2027 numbers while Search decelerates.

thesis.point: The equity stakes and base rates add a right tail at little cost.
thesis.evidence: SpaceX is about $82B (551M shares at $148.68, $14.1B locked until Q3 2027) and Anthropic is carried at $124.3B on a $47.6B cost. A reported November IPO at about $2T would add roughly $5-11/sh after tax. Separately, 9 of 10 prior 15% drawdowns were higher a year later; the one exception required EPS to fall 19%.

memo.variant_view: There is no strong variant view; this is a modest long. We sit between two consensuses. Our $371.53 target is well below the sell side (49 analysts, mean $425.45, median $425, range $310-515, Strong Buy), because we apply about 22x NTM core EPS and haircut for 2027 capex, negative FCF and the $84.75B equity program, which the Street's ~$425 largely looks through. We are slightly above the options market: its distribution centers on $358.96 with P(gain) 0.554 and a 15th percentile of $247.69, against our $371.53, P(gain) 0.593 and $256.52. Our small premium to the options market comes from the fact-checked EPS revision trend and the stake/IPO optionality. The difference is about 3.5% of price, which is not enough to call it a mispricing.

valuation.methods: Supervisor-reconciled research target (12m) of $367 (range across five agents $360-375). The main method is NTM core P/E: about 22x on NTM core EPS of about $16.2-16.9 at the Sept 2027 horizon gives $356-372. Added to that are about $13-15/sh of after-tax stake value (SpaceX corrected to about $82B; Anthropic at its $124.3B carrying value) plus about $4-5/sh of probability-weighted Anthropic IPO uplift. A rolled-forward SOTP (about $370) is the cross-check. DCF cross-checks at $313-340 reflect the ~$257B 2027 capex consensus and are weighted about 20%. The published target of $371.53 is the median of the blended options/forecaster distribution, weighted 67% market and 33% forecasters; the expected value is $391.56 (+14.2%).

catalysts.event: Joint proposed Final Judgment due in the DOJ ad-tech case (court-ordered 30-day deadline after Judge Brinkema's Sept 2 remedies ruling; no AdX divestiture)
catalysts.why_it_moves: It locks in behavioral-only remedies (Prebid interoperability, bid-data sharing, a 6-year monitor) and removes the breakup tail. Most of this is already priced after Sept 2.
catalysts.watch: Disputed provisions submitted separately, the scope of the worldwide AdX rival-access terms, and Google's notice of appeal.

catalysts.date: Oct-Dec 2026 (Google says 'much earlier' than year-end; October rumored)
catalysts.event: Gemini 4 release (replaces the delayed Gemini 3.5 Pro)
catalysts.why_it_moves: This is the first test of model leadership after DeepMind talent departures and the Meta Muse launch. A strong launch would ease the 'Search gets disintermediated' fear; a slip or weak benchmarks would feed it.
catalysts.watch: Release date versus the October chatter, head-to-head benchmarks against OpenAI/Anthropic/Meta models, and Gemini app MAU and AI Mode usage disclosed alongside it.

catalysts.event: Q3 2026 earnings. Consensus core EPS is about $3.02 and revenue about $127B. Alphabet IR has not yet announced the call date.
catalysts.why_it_moves: This is the first print since Meta Muse and the $84.75B raise, and the first official color on 2027 capex. Q2 showed that a capex surprise alone can move the stock down on a beat.
catalysts.watch: Search & other growth against Q2's +17% (single digits would signal a thesis break), paid-click trends, Cloud growth and the $514B backlog, any early 2027 capex framing against the ~$257B consensus, FCF after Q2's -$5.9B, ATM usage beyond sell-to-cover, and the GAAP SpaceX mark-to-market loss (excluded from core EPS).

catalysts.event: Meta Q3 2026 earnings: first quantified read on Muse agent engagement
catalysts.why_it_moves: Muse was the trigger for GOOGL's 3% drop on Sept 23. Strong Muse usage or commerce-query data would reinforce the Search-disintermediation narrative, while weak adoption would ease it.
catalysts.watch: Muse DAU/MAU, agentic shopping or query volume, and Meta's 2027 capex guide (a read-across on AI capex tolerance).

catalysts.event: Anthropic IPO at a reported ~$2T valuation, raising up to ~$100B
catalysts.why_it_moves: The IPO would re-mark Alphabet's stake, now carried at $124.3B on a $47.6B cost, and disclose the ownership percentage (estimated at 10-15%). That is about +$5-11/sh after tax at $2T. A slip or a lower price would remove part of the right tail.
catalysts.watch: A public S-1 flip (it typically comes about 15 days before the roadshow), Alphabet's disclosed ownership, the pricing range against $2T, and first-day trading.

catalysts.date: Oct 9, Oct 24 and Dec 8, 2026 (remaining SPCX insider lock-up tranches; Dec 8 is the final 180-day release)
catalysts.event: SpaceX lock-up tranche expiries
catalysts.why_it_moves: Alphabet's ~551M SPCX shares (about $82B) move with SPCX. A 20% SPCX drop costs roughly $1.3/sh pre-tax, so this is a stake-value nuisance, not a thesis driver.
catalysts.watch: SPCX price reaction around each tranche. Alphabet's $14.1B long-term restricted block stays locked until Q3 2027.

catalysts.date: Q4 2026 - Q1 2027 (oral argument not yet scheduled; Google's reply brief due Sept 29)
catalysts.event: DC Circuit oral argument in the search monopoly appeal (Google appeals liability and remedies; DOJ cross-appeals for a default-payment ban and Chrome divestiture)
catalysts.why_it_moves: The argument itself only moves sentiment through the panel's questions. The ruling, likely mid-2027 or later, sets whether the Apple default payments and Chrome are at risk.
catalysts.watch: The scheduling order, panel composition, and the panel's questions on the payment ban and Chrome.

catalysts.event: Q4 2026 earnings with the formal 2027 capex guide
catalysts.why_it_moves: This is the single biggest swing factor. The FactSet consensus is about $257B (Evercore $262B). A guide far above that, with FCF negative into 2028 and more equity issuance, is the main path to the $250 thesis break. A guide at or below consensus paired with visible Cloud returns would re-rate the stock.
catalysts.watch: 2027 capex against $257B, depreciation guide, FCF trajectory, whether buybacks resume, and Cloud operating margin.

risks.risk: Agentic assistants (Meta Muse, ChatGPT) take commercial queries, and Search growth falls from +17% to single digits, causing an actual EPS downgrade rather than multiple noise.
risks.signpost: Search & other growth below ~10% in the Q3 or Q4 print, decelerating paid clicks, strong Muse engagement numbers from Meta on Oct 28, and FY2027 EPS revisions turning net negative.

risks.risk: The capex/FCF spiral: the 2027 guide lands well above ~$257B, depreciation compresses margins, FCF stays negative and the $40B ATM or more equity dilutes beyond sell-to-cover.
risks.signpost: Q3 commentary pre-guiding 2027 capex well above $257B, another negative-FCF quarter, and ATM issuance well above RSU tax-withholding levels in the 10-Q.

risks.risk: An AI-valuation reset removes the stake credit: the Anthropic IPO slips or prices well below $2T, and SPCX keeps falling.
risks.signpost: No public S-1 by early November, a price range well below $2T, or SPCX breaking below about $120 (from $148.68).

risks.risk: Model competitiveness slips (Gemini 4 delay, DeepMind talent losses), undermining both Search defense and Cloud/TPU demand.
risks.signpost: Gemini 4 slipping into 2027 or trailing rival models on launch benchmarks, and further senior DeepMind departures.

trade.position: 2 sh (~$686, 6.9% of the $10,000 book); supervisor cap 12%. Size was set by the joint portfolio solve (overlap with AVGO, META and SPY), not by the stop budget.
trade.entry: Two tranches per the supervisor: buy 1 share now near $342.75 and 1 share after the Q3 2026 report (expected Oct 27). The second tranche goes in only if FY2027 core EPS revisions stay positive and there is no capex pre-guide far above the ~$257B consensus. A close below $250 cancels it.
trade.exit_or_add: Exit at the $256.52 stop (15th percentile), and in any case on a close below the $250 thesis break, which is about 17x FY2027 EPS with no stake credit. Take profit at $465.33. Add up to the 12% cap if Q3 shows Search at 12% or higher with Cloud backlog growing, or if the Feb 2027 capex guide is at or below about $257B with a credible FCF path. Also exit if the capex guide comes in far above consensus with FCF guided negative through 2028. [Updated 2026-11-19: the one upside exit is now $324.06, where the 12-month expected value no longer beats the 4% cash sleeve and the model sells every share; any other take-profit figure in this memo is superseded.]
trade.take_profit_note: expected value: the price where the 12-month expected return (research fixed in dollars, options leg moving with the price) falls to the 4% cash rate (full exit) (as of 2026-11-19)

what_changes_our_mind: Search & other growth prints in single digits in Q3 or Q4 2026 while FY2027 EPS revisions turn net negative (the 2022 pattern). That would be a thesis break, and we would exit.
A February 2027 capex guide well above ~$257B (for example $280B+) with FCF negative into 2028 and further equity issuance. We would cut the position.

Upside case: Anthropic prices at or above $2T in November, Alphabet discloses 14% or more ownership, and Q3 shows Cloud backlog above $514B with stable margins. We would add to the 12% cap and raise the research target (12m).

inputs_detail.derivation: FY27 consensus of $2.06 grown about 31%, close to the consensus FY26-to-FY27 growth (+36%, $1.52 to $2.06) with a little fade. Q2 non-GAAP EPS of $0.42 and the $0.38 Q3 guide [3] already annualize to about $1.60, which supports the trajectory.

Set above NVDA (28x) and TSMC's 10-year average (about 23x) [4] because Intel's EPS is growing off a depressed base and supply is constrained. It is well below today's 58-62x FY27 [4][1]. Intel's own history (P/S 1.5-12.5x over a decade [5]) shows peak multiples do not last, and the 2000 peak at about 50x EPS was followed by an 82% drawdown [19].

Consensus EPS is on roughly 5.40B diluted shares (5,285M basic after the full greenshoe [6][22] plus 119M RSUs/PSUs). I add about 50M of the 143M DoC escrow shares, which are released as Secure Enclave disbursements arrive [22]. That is a ~1% haircut. The phantom ~$15B follow-on I counted in round 1 is removed.

agents.reasoning: Round-2 revision. I verified the supervisor's main correction in the primary filings. There is no planned ~$15B follow-on: $15B was the proposed size of the August deal [23], which was upsized to $20B [24], and the 31.6M-share greenshoe was exercised on Aug 11 [6]. That leaves 5,285M basic shares and $22.62B net proceeds [22], and EDGAR shows no later offering filing [25]. The 424B5 also lists $15.6B of NCI and 143M escrow shares [22], which I had left out. Net effect on fair value: removing the phantom dilution helps, while the NCI, the higher H2 net debt and the escrow shares hurt, so fair value goes from $99 to $96. Starting point is unchanged: INTC is $120 after +258% in a year and +34% in September, at about 58x FY27 consensus EPS of $2.06 and about 11x sales, near the top of its decade P/S range [1][2][4][5]. Base rates (own computation, 28 large semis/tech names [17]): after a +150% trailing year the median next-12-month return was +48% (n=243), or +25% for the post-2002 ex-mega-winner subset (n=72), with a log SD of 0.63-0.82 and about 19% of cases losing more than 30%. Survivorship bias is heavy, so I cut the momentum drift to about 0-10%. Valuation pulls the other way: fair value of about $96 is 20% below spot, and Intel's 2000 peak at about 50x was followed by -82% [19]. Sell-side consensus of about $116, with 32 of 48 at Hold [1][10], agrees with a flat-to-down center. Manifold's 41% on touching $150 by end-2026 [15] is a bit below a driftless touch model (~55%). Per the source review, I now give no weight to the thin 2027 Polymarket markets (~$10k volume) [11][13]. That removes a little of the bear tail I had attributed to macro. Removing the supply overhang of a phantom follow-on is a small positive for the 12-month path. Together these move my median from $112 to $113. I keep sigma at 0.65 (between the base-rate sample's 0.63-0.82 and slightly below the 76% realized vol, since vol mean-reverts after spikes). Result: P(>=120) is 46%, P(>=60) is 84%, and P(>=300) is 7%. The scenario mean (0.25x$60 + 0.5x$110 + 0.25x$185 = $116) is consistent. I agree with the supervisor's factual corrections. I keep my own ladder rather than the forecaster mean because my base-rate evidence still argues for fatter tails on both sides. Research limits: round-1 data constraints (Twelve Data paywall, Alpha Vantage rate limit) still apply, and round 2 used 7 targeted fetches (EDGAR, 424B5, 8-K, Intel IR).

agents.reasoning: Per-share figures are per CURRENT pre-split share (today's Class A share plus the Class C share it gets in the Jan-2027 dividend; 8-K 2026-10-21); EV is unchanged by the dividend. Evidence, mostly primary: Q3-26 release, 10-Q and call; Q2-26 call; nine prior releases for the guidance record. The core is strong: revenue +26% (impressions +10%, price +14%), Q4 guide $73-76B (+22-27%), and Meta beat the top of its range in 6 of 8 quarters. The debate is cost: FY26 expenses $175-179B (incl. $12.3B legal), capex $135-145B, $454.5B of non-cancelable commitments ($121.4B due 2027), management 'investing aggressively' in 2027, and RL loss ~$15B. Driver build: FY27 revenue $312B (at consensus) from impressions +9% and price +10% plus new AI revenue; FoA margin 51.6% FY25 -> 37.8% FY27 -> 34.5% FY28 as D&A rises with capex that follows the AI capex file ($192B, $236B; above street). FY27 EPS ~$32 (~5% below consensus $33.9). Valuation: SOTP $750 (FoA 16.5x NTM EBIT, RL -$25B), P/E 20x $691, EV/EBITDA 10x $681 -> research target (12m) $715.83, +11% vs $642.62. Scenarios: bear $409 (25%), base $716 (50%), bull $1,019 (25%). Ladder: 75% this scenario mix (within-scenario vol 17-18%) plus 25% a market-anchored lognormal (median $650, sigma 33%, about the stock's 43% realized vol trimmed for non-earnings periods), since price is the best single forecast. That gives a median of ~$697 and P(>= $643) = 0.59. Not driver-linked: the RL venture value (-$25B), the litigation and investment adjustments, and RL revenue. agents.reasoning: Per-share figures are per CURRENT pre-split share (today's Class A share plus the Class C share it receives on 2027-01-19); EV is unchanged by the dividend. Industry lane: the rest of the ad chain says demand is still strong but slowing. WARC's Q3-26 outlook has social ad spend +21.3% in 2026 and +14.6% in 2027, total +11.9% then +8.4% [13]; IAB US social +16.5% in 2026 [14]; Google Search +17%, YouTube +13%, Amazon ads +26%, Reddit ads +64%, Pinterest +18%, Snap ads only +9% in Q2-26 [16-20]; eMarketer puts Meta's 2026 ad revenue at ~$242B [30]. Meta's own impressions growth fell from +19% (Q1) to +10% (Q3) while price per ad rose to +14% [6][5][1]; an agency newsletter reports large CPM rises [31] (lead only, low weight). On the cost side the supply chain says Meta's bill keeps rising: CoreWeave $21B through 2032 [21], Nebius $12B from early 2027 [22], DRAM contract prices still rising [23], neocloud rental pricing up >50% YTD (MS proprietary index, used only as direction) [25], $454.5B of non-cancelable commitments and $355.7B of leases not yet commenced [2]. So the driver build has FY2027 revenue +17.7% (impressions +8%, price +9%), 2.4% under consensus, and FoA margin falling to 37.4% as D&A rises to $47B; FY2027 EPS ~$31 vs $33.92 consensus. Capex follows the AI-capex file base ($141B in 2026, $192B in 2027) [24]. Guidance record: five straight quarterly revenue guides at or above the range (median +3.4% vs midpoint), expense guides inside, capex guides overshot in 2024-25. Valuation: SOTP (FoA 16x EV/EBIT, RL separately at -$94B), P/E 19x and EV/EBITDA 10.5x give a research target (12m) of $691 after -$19.9B accrued legal and -$10.5B probability-weighted litigation. Ladder: bear $455 / base $680 / bull $920 at 25/50/25 with 25% within-scenario vol (total ~35% log vol vs 43% realized); the centre (~$670 median) sits between the price and the research target because the price is the better one-year predictor. No option data used. Research limited: Q3-26 peer results (Alphabet, Snap, Pinterest, Reddit) are not out yet; X/Twitter not used; no prediction market found on a Meta event that matters (Kalshi lists only headcount contracts). In-lane sources: 19 of 31.

inputs_detail.derivation: Mid-cycle margin from Marvell's own record: FY25 non-GAAP operating margin 28.9% and FY26 35.3% (Q4 FY26 release), H1 FY27 35.9% ((846.9 + 1,003.2) / (2,417.8 + 2,739.3), Q1/Q2 FY27 releases): mean (28.9 + 35.3 + 35.9)/3 = 33.4%, rounded 33.5%. Revenue: average of model FY28 (19,600) and FY29 (28,200) = 23,900, not FY29 alone (round 1), since FY29 is a growth year and includes a 14-week Q4. EPS = 23,900 x 0.335 x 0.86 / 928M = $7.42 (driver-linked) x 24x = $178. Through-cycle P/E 24x = peer lower quartile (NVDA 16.5, AVGO 20.8, COHR 24.3, CRDO 25.8; median of the four 22.6x, rounded up for MRVL growth). Weight 0.3 (playbook 0.2-0.4; judgment, untested). Netflix's US price steps came in Jan 2025 and spring 2026 (sources 6, 4), ~15 months apart, so we place the next one in early 2028: Q1'28 +5.5%, Q2-Q3'28 +7.0%, Q4'28 +6.5% (ads maturing). agents.reasoning: Skeptic lane. The downside evidence is broad and current. Revenue growth has slowed four quarters running (Q1'26 16.2%, Q2 13.4%, Q3 11.8%, Q4 guide 11.5%). The FY26 range ended below its first midpoint. Ad revenue was cut 10% ($3.0B -> $2.7B). YouTube has twice Netflix's US TV time (Nielsen, August). HSBC, Wells Fargo, Needham and Wolfe downgraded, a Seeking Alpha Sell followed, and hedge-fund holders fell (146 -> 121). Credit is not a risk: net debt is 6.9B on about 16B of EBITDA, the July 2026 10-year priced at 5.25%, and the revolver covenant is 3x EBITDA/interest, well clear. Weighed honestly, the business is still growing about 11% with a 31.5% margin and buying back about 5% of its shares a year, so the risk is a de-rating and estimate cuts, not distress. Model: four regional drivers built from price (the March-2026 US rise laps in Q2'27), members (flat to +1% in the US) and the 2027 ad-tier launches, with no currency gain carried forward. FY27 revenue comes to 55.4B (+8.5%), 2.1% below the Street's 56.6B. Content-amortization leverage is limited (cost ratio -0.3 points), so the EBIT margin is 32.4% in FY27 and 33.1% in FY28. Downside and upside move the drivers (revenue levels -6%/+3.5%, cost ratios +2.5/-1.5 points) and the multiple (-4.0/+4.5 turns); the downside sits further from base, a fatter left tail. agents.reasoning: Start: the stock is at $59.68, down 46% in a year, at 16.3x NTM consensus EPS. The fall followed three things: revenue growth slowing each quarter (16% -> 13% -> 12% -> ~11.5% guided for Q4), the cut to the 2026 ad target ($3.0B -> $2.7B), and evidence of weaker engagement. Lane work (alternative data) tested whether the engagement worry is real. It is, but it shows up mostly in volume, not yet in churn. Apptopia (via Bloomberg/A.V. Club) has US subscribers not opening the app up 16.6% y/y in Q3. Nielsen's Gauge (TheWrap, Tubefilter) puts Netflix at 7.7% of US TV against YouTube's record 15.8%. The Entertainment Strategy Guy and Hub Intel Substack show returning shows losing audiences and per-user viewing falling. Stocktwits retail sentiment is extremely bearish. On the other side, Antenna data still shows strong Premium uptake among cord-cutters, and the company says price rises in the US, Mexico and Spain went as expected. My read: pricing still works but member growth is saturating, so the base case decelerates memberships (+4.6% in 2026, +3.5%, +2.8%) and keeps ARM at +3-3.5%, below the 2026 pace. Ads come from company statements (250M+ monthly active ad viewers, 15 new markets in 2027), not the stale Omdia path, which I reconciled. Guidance record: quarterly revenue beats have shrunk to about zero in 2026 and margin beats came from expense timing, so Q4 sits just under the guide. Content cost (+7.5%/+6.5%) and opex give 33.0%/34.1% margins. EPS ends 2-3% under consensus. Valuation follows the playbook: P/E on our own GAAP EPS with the k = 0.8 shrink toward a thin 3-name whole-company peer median (17.66x), giving 16.59x and $69.32 (+16%). That is mostly buyback-driven EPS growth at a flat multiple. Downside (P10, $42.24) has the engagement slide turning into churn, an ad slip, a content push and a de-rating to ~13.6x. Upside (P90, $102.86) has ads and pricing working and a partial return of the premium. Engine-sized judgment calls over 5% are listed in gap_note for Kilian. Research used about 25 searches and fetches; X/Twitter, Reddit and several data-vendor pages (Apptopia, MediaPost/Antenna, Puck, eMarketer, MarketBeat) blocked fetching, so I relied on reachable relays of them and flagged each relay. No option prices were consulted.

memo.title: NFLX: small two-step long in a de-rated cash compounder at ~18x 2027 EPS; the Oct 20 print and the January 2027 guide settle the engagement debate
memo.call_reason: The published 12-month target of $75.49 is 8.5% above the $69.58 close and the research target (12m) of $80.00 is 15.0% above it, at medium conviction; size is capped by the supervisor at ~8% because the engagement debate is unresolved and earnings are three weeks out.
memo.one_liner: Netflix has de-rated to ~18x 2027 consensus EPS on an engagement scare that has not yet reached churn (2% vs a 4% industry average) or pricing, while recurring FCF of ~$11.3-11.7B and a ~3-4% annual share shrink keep compounding per-share value. We buy 11 shares in two tranches around the Oct 20 print, target $75.49 / research target (12m) $80, take profit $97.77, stop at the $51 thesis break.

thesis.point: 1. Per-share cash compounding is intact and is being bought back cheaply.
thesis.evidence: Recurring 2026 FCF is ~$11.3-11.7B (the $11B pre-fee guide incl. the ~$700M Brazil deposit, vs $12.5B including the after-tax WBD fee), implying ~$13.0-13.5B in 2027. Net debt is only $5.24B (A2/A), and Q2 buybacks retired 52.9M shares, shrinking the 4.164B count ~3-4% a year.

thesis.point: 2. Monetisation shows no damage from the engagement debate yet.
thesis.evidence: Antenna July churn is 2% vs a 4% average for major services; the 2026 upfront nearly doubled ad commitments and the ad tier passed 250M monthly active viewers, with ads ~$3B in 2026. The fall season (~40% of annual gross adds) is the next test.

thesis.point: 3. The multiple already discounts a lot; the bar for the print is low.
thesis.evidence: At $69.58 the stock trades ~18x 2027 consensus EPS of $3.82 with 2028 at $4.56, near Wells Fargo's 15x bear multiple ($57 PT) after Wells Fargo and HSBC downgrades in September. Our research target (12m) of $80 needs only ~19x NTM EPS of ~$4.25 and a 4.5% FCF yield, not a return to the old 30x+.

memo.variant_view: We sit between the two consensus views. The options market's distribution (result.json market_only) is centred at $70.19 with P(gain) 0.51, i.e. it prices no edge; we have $75.49 and P(gain) 0.58 because the forecasters see churn, ad growth and buybacks absorbing the engagement drag. The sell-side is far more bullish (weighted median PT $95, Deutsche Bank upgrade to Buy at $95 on 9/29, Wells Fargo $57 underweight); we stay well below it because peer de-ratings of quality large caps (DIS, PYPL, NKE, ADBE) have a median ~-6% follow-through over the next 12 months, so we do not underwrite a re-rating before the January 2027 guide. The real variant view is modest: the market is treating an engagement metric (Nielsen 7.8% share vs YouTube 14.2%; Wells Fargo ~-4% y/y hours per member in H2'26) as if it were already a revenue problem.

valuation.methods: Supervisor research target (12m) $80 (five forecasters $77-83, mean $80.3) = 60/40 blend of (a) P/E: NTM EPS at Sep-2027 of 0.25x$3.82 + 0.75x$4.56 = $4.38, less ~3% engagement haircut = $4.25, at 19x = ~$81; and (b) FCF: NTM FCF ~$14.5B at a 4.5% yield, less $5.24B net debt, over ~4.08B diluted shares = ~$77.7. The published 12-month target ($75.49, the median of the blended market/forecaster distribution) sits below the research target (12m) because the options market centres near spot; take profit $97.77 is the 75th percentile, stop $51 is the thesis break (~13.4x 2027 EPS, ~6.6% FCF yield).

catalysts.event: Paramount Skydance closes its WBD acquisition (all regulatory conditions met in Aug; 12-state AG settlement Sep 21)
catalysts.why_it_moves: Creates a combined HBO Max/Paramount+ rival with ~$80B of debt; integration plans and bundling/pricing signal how hard it will compete for subscribers and content.
catalysts.watch: Streaming bundle/pricing announcements, content-spend guidance and leverage of the combined company.

catalysts.event: First Nielsen Gauge on the recalibrated methodology (ARF DASH universe), covering the start of the fall TV season
catalysts.why_it_moves: Nielsen share (7.8% vs YouTube 14.2% in July) is the core of the bear case; a further drop under the new method would be read as confirmation even though it is a methodology break.
catalysts.watch: Netflix share of TV time vs the July 7.8% and YouTube's lead; any restatement of history under the new method.

catalysts.event: Q3 2026 results and Q4 guide (letter 1:01pm PT, video interview 1:45pm PT)
catalysts.why_it_moves: First print since the September downgrades; the Q4 guide and any 2027 framing set the growth path the multiple hangs on. Q2's slight beat with a lower outlook sent the stock down after hours.
catalysts.watch: Revenue vs $12.86B guide, 33.2% operating margin, EPS $0.82; Q4 guide vs the $51.2B / 31.5% FY26 plan; engagement and ad-revenue commentary; Q3 buyback pace and FCF vs the ~$12.5B FY guide; early 2027 growth/margin framing (~10% growth, 33-34% margin needed).

catalysts.event: Antenna churn and sign-up reads through the fall acquisition season
catalysts.why_it_moves: Churn at 2% is the evidence that engagement loss has not reached monetisation; Sep-Dec is ~40% of annual gross adds, so a rise here would validate the bear case.
catalysts.watch: Netflix monthly churn above ~2.5%; gross adds vs prior years; ad-tier mix.

catalysts.event: NFL Thanksgiving Eve game on Netflix (Packers at Rams), first of its kind
catalysts.why_it_moves: Live-sports tentpoles drive sign-ups and ad inventory and counter the engagement narrative; a streaming failure would hurt.
catalysts.watch: Reported viewership, stream stability, ad sell-out.

catalysts.event: Fury vs. Joshua heavyweight fight streamed live on Netflix (reported by trade/fan press, not yet verified in a company release)
catalysts.why_it_moves: A global live event at no extra cost; another engagement and sign-up spike for Q4.
catalysts.watch: Concurrent viewers; Q4 net-add commentary in January.

catalysts.event: NFL Christmas Day doubleheader exclusively on Netflix
catalysts.why_it_moves: Highest-profile ad inventory of the year; supports the ad-scaling leg of the thesis.
catalysts.watch: Viewership vs 2025 Christmas games; advertiser demand.

catalysts.event: Q4 2026 results and first full-year 2027 revenue, margin and FCF guidance
catalysts.why_it_moves: The main re-rating or de-rating event: ~10% 2027 growth with 33-34% margin supports the $80 research target (12m); high-single-digit growth or a flat margin is the bear path toward the $51 thesis break.
catalysts.watch: 2027 revenue growth vs ~10%, operating margin vs 33-34%, 2027 FCF vs ~$13.0-13.5B, buyback size, ad-revenue target.

catalysts.event: H2 2026 'What We Watched' engagement report
catalysts.why_it_moves: Direct test of Wells Fargo's ~-4% y/y hours-per-member call for H2'26.
catalysts.watch: Total hours and hours per member y/y; share of views from top titles.

risks.risk: Engagement erosion reaches churn and pricing power (YouTube and creators taking TV time).
risks.signpost: Antenna churn above ~2.5% for two consecutive months, Netflix share falling further on the recalibrated Gauge, or a weaker take-rate on the next price increase.

risks.risk: The January 2027 guide shows high-single-digit growth and a stalled margin, cutting 2027/28 EPS.

tax_assumptions._future_note: Combined rate you'd expect on today's embedded gains when you'd otherwise sell (15% federal + ~6% state once working). Drives the sell cost and the gain-harvest suggestion.
tax_assumptions._tax_note: Kilian 2026-09-28: taxable account; ~$20,000 internship wages in 2026 plus realized gains; claimed as a dependent by a parent living in CA; full-time student under 24 living in CT. Assumed (not confirmed): domicile stays CA (a student living away at school keeps the parents' domicile, FTB Pub 1031), CT dorm is not a permanent place of abode so CT does not tax investment income; kiddie tax applies (earned income not more than half of his support). Federal 2026 figures from IRS Rev. Proc. 2025-32; CA brackets are 2025 (FTB Tax News Oct 2025), 2026's not published yet.
tax_assumptions._other_unearned_note: Dividends etc. this year (rough: GOOGL + META dividends). Counts toward the kiddie-tax threshold.
tax_assumptions._kiddie_note: Unearned income above $2,700 (2 x $1,350, Rev. Proc. 2025-32) is taxed at the parent's rate, federal (Form 8615) and CA (FTB 3800). Applies to a full-time student 19-23 whose earned income is not more than half of his own support.
tax_assumptions._parent_note: Kilian 2026-10-20 22:04Z: parent in NYC, 37% federal bracket. Parent's NY/NYC rates do not apply to Kilian's gains (no NY kiddie tax under Form 8615).
tax_assumptions._flat_note: Kilian 2026-10-20 22:04Z: the parent claiming him lives in New York City (37% federal bracket; NY 9.65%, NYC 3.876% at the parent's income). Federal kiddie tax (Form 8615): unearned income above kiddie_threshold ($2,700) at the parent's federal rates, short-term 37%, long-term 20% (the 37% bracket is above the 20% LTCG start, Rev. Proc. 2025-32); up to the threshold at Kilian's own federal rates, 10% short-term (wages $20k less the $16,100 dependent standard deduction leave ~$3.9k taxable, inside the 10% band to $12,400) and 0% long-term. New York has no kiddie tax when Form 8615 is used: the child's investment income is reported on the child's own NY return and taxed at the child's own rates (NYS IT-201-I, 'Does your child have investment income over $2,700?'). So NY and NYC tax every gain at Kilian's own marginal rates: NY 5.40% ($13,900-80,650) + NYC 3.762% ($12,000-25,000), single, 2026 schedules (NYS IT-2105-I 2026); NY dependent standard deduction $3,100. Assumed: Kilian is domiciled at the parent's NYC home (a dependent student keeps the parents' domicile) and his CT dorm is not a permanent place of abode. NIIT dropped (Kilian 2026-10-21 00:48Z 'yes you may drop it'; it was kept per his 2026-10-01 20:32Z ask): Form 8960 applies it on the child's own MAGI over $200,000 (single), which his income does not reach. Short-term = 37% + 9.162% = 46.162%; long-term = 20% + 9.162% = 29.162%; own rates under the threshold 19.162% / 9.162%. Was CA (41.3% / 28.1% / 14% / 2%) until 2026-10-20. Net losses offset gains; up to $3,000 deducts at the own short-term rate. Bracket mode (mode 'brackets') still holds the CA schedule and is not updated.
tax_assumptions._short_term_all_note: Kilian 2026-10-28 card 'Assume short-term on all' (thread 'Fix AMAT target vs sell mismatch'): every holding is assumed sold within the year at the short-term rate, so a trim only pays the same tax H years sooner; band per year = q tau (1 - (1+d)^-H) / H + spread / T. Overrides lot_aware_horizon; false restores it.
tax_assumptions._lot_aware_note: Kilian 2026-10-20 card 'Lot-aware' (Assumption audit thread): a short-term lot's trim band compares selling now with holding it to its one-year date and selling long-term: band per year = q (tau_now - flat_long_term_rate (1+d)^-X) / X, X = years until the oldest (FIFO) lot turns long-term (floor 1 day), plus spread / T. Long-term lots keep the T-year rule (years_until_you_would_otherwise_sell, future_rate_on_deferred_gains, Claude defaults 2026-09-28). false restores the T-year rule for every lot.

agents.method_text: Blend of 16x consistent-basis NTM EPS at Oct-2027 (Q3 FY28-Q2 FY29 ~$17.5) = $280 (60%) and a 5.0% FCF yield on ~$300B NTM FCF plus $57B of net cash and haircut equity stakes over 23.8B shares = $255 (40%); blended ~$270. Break-even multiple on $17.5 is 13.5x, so 16x already absorbs ~17% further de-rating from today's 19.3-19.5x.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: Consistent NTM EPS at Oct-2027 (Q3 FY28-Q2 FY29) ~$17.5 x 16x; break-even 13.5x

inputs_detail.derivation: Consensus $15.68 (range $9.80-$18.75). Cross-checked bottom-up: FY27 revenue ~$404B (Q1 $81.6B + Q2 $96.2B + Q3 guide $108B + Q4 ~$118B) x 1.70 per management's ~70% FY28 growth guide = ~$686B; GM 72.5% (FY28 guide 72-73%); opex ~$50B; tax 17%; ~23.9B diluted shares = ~$15.6.

Sharp deceleration from +70% because FY28 is supply-constrained and hyperscaler capex already guided to ~$1.3T in 2027 with FCF thinning (Meta) and component inflation (MSFT/Meta) absorbing budget; Wells Fargo capex-math caution cited in source 9.

inputs_detail.input: NTM EPS at 2027-10-05 (Q3 FY28 + Q4 FY28 + Q1 FY29 + Q2 FY29)
inputs_detail.derivation: Same window construction as today's 19.3x (next four unreported quarters). H2 FY28 = FY28 $15.7 - Q1 FY28 $3.17 - Q2 FY28 $3.63 = $8.90 (quarterly consensus, source 12); H1 FY29 ~$8.6-8.9 assuming FY29 +15% with quarters flattening off the Q4 FY28 run-rate. Total ~$17.5 (supervisor range $17.4-17.8 for FY29 +10-20%). Round 1 used Q4 FY28-Q3 FY29, one quarter shifted.

Below NVDA's current ~19.3-19.5x on the same NTM basis and far below the peer median ~35x: by Oct-2027 forward growth decelerates from +70% toward ~15%, and the market prices peak-cycle risk (MU at 6x is the extreme). Inside the 6-129x peer range; below AVGO/TSM ~20.5x because NVDA's post-FY28 growth is more cyclical and customer-concentrated. Break-even is 13.5x ($236.88/$17.5), so 16x embeds ~2.5 turns of further compression but not a 31% de-rating. Kept at 16x rather than the supervisor's 16.5x: compression has been estimate-driven so far, but by the horizon the estimates themselves will be decelerating, removing that support.

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: NTM FCF ~$300B (72% of ~$416B NI) at 5.0% yield + $23.2B net cash + $34.2B haircut equity stakes, 23.8B shares

inputs_detail.derivation: H1 FY27 FCF $69.9B vs non-GAAP NI ~$99B (~70%); Q2 alone $21.3B FCF vs $54.0B non-GAAP NI as receivables jumped to $63.1B (DSO 60 vs 45) and inventory to $31.6B. Assume modest improvement to 72%.
$17.5 consistent-basis NTM EPS x ~23.8B shares.

Cash $22.443B + marketable debt securities $34.143B - debt $33.366B ($1.0B short-term + $32.366B long-term) per 10-Q balance sheet. Round 1 wrongly included $42.8B of marketable equity securities as cash.

10-Q: marketable equity securities $42.783B (Level 1 $31.977B publicly held; Level 2 $10.806B unregistered warrants/preferred; $36.9B under short-term lock-ups, $5.0B locked through Dec-2027) at a 50% haircut = $21.4B; non-marketable equity securities $51.157B at a 75% haircut = $12.8B. Haircuts reflect lock-ups, AI-valuation volatility and that some stakes are in customers (circularity).

AVGO and TSM trade ~20.5x forward EPS (~4.9% earnings yield). At 72% conversion a 16x P/E corresponds to a 4.5% FCF yield; I require 5.0% (~13.9x P/E equivalent) because the cash leg should carry the working-capital and receivables-concentration risk (DSO 60, terms up to one year), which is why this leg sits below the P/E leg.
24.285B diluted Q2 FY27 less ~400M/yr repurchased (203M in H1 FY27) plus SBC dilution.

agents.reasoning: Round 2. Primary documents show an extraordinary ramp: Q2 FY27 revenue $96.2B (+106% y/y), non-GAAP EPS $2.22, Q3 guide $108B, and a call guide of ~70% FY28 revenue growth, supply-constrained, with GM settling at 72-73% (verified verbatim by the supervisor). Bottom-up FY28 EPS ~$15.6 matches consensus $15.7. The supervisor found two errors that I verified and fixed: (1) net cash is $23.2B, not $66B: I re-read the 10-Q balance sheet and $42.8B of 'marketable securities' are equity stakes (Level 1 $32.0B, Level 2 $10.8B, mostly locked up); I now add them separately at a 50% haircut, plus non-marketable stakes ($51.2B) at 75%; (2) my horizon NTM EPS was shifted one quarter; on the consistent Q3 FY28-Q2 FY29 window (verified quarterly consensus $2.47/$2.73/$3.17/$3.63 for the current NTM, so H2 FY28 = $8.90) it is ~$17.5, slightly above my round-1 $17.3 because my round-1 build had decelerated quarters too sharply. Today's 19.3x is on $12.00-12.25; the 17x and 14.8x quotes are later windows, so I compress from 19.3x not 17x. agents.reasoning: Base rates first. NVDA's own 12-month forward returns since 2002: median +40%, P(down) 22%, P(<-40%) 7%; in setups like today (prior year +10-45%, at a 52-week high, n=25) median +29%. That record is survivorship-biased for a $5.7T leader; the top-dog base rate (Arnott/Wu: largest companies trail their sector by ~4%/yr) and a ~7% market return pull the centre to roughly +5-12%. Round-2 corrections from the supervisor, all accepted: (1) my horizon NTM EPS used a window shifted one quarter forward; on the same Q3 FY28-Q2 FY29 window as today's 19.3-19.7x it is ~$16.7 after a 5% haircut (also FY29 growth trimmed to +15% given consensus 2027 capex growth of only ~+22%, src 27); (2) my fair value used 18x while my base scenario used 15x; I now use one multiple, 16x, in both; (3) FCF conversion of 85% is not supported (Q2 FY27 FCF 36-39% of NI, H1 ~70%), now 75%, with ~$1/share true net cash; (4) the 10Y at 5.24-5.28% is verified at Treasury (src 26) but it is the highest since 2007, not 2002; (5) the Fed-odds source was misattributed; the Dec-9 meeting-specific Kalshi contract shows ~70% for a 25bp hike (search-result snapshot; direct fetch 429) and DeFi Rate 72%, so the macro headwind stands; (6) I dropped the 'historical 17-20x floor' argument. On compression: it has been estimate-driven (FY28 EPS +24% in 90 days while the price rose), so it is real but has not hurt holders; I assume 3.5 more turns (to 16x), while a flat year needs ~14.2x on my EPS, a de-rating that likely needs an EPS break. Fair value $255 (P/E $267, FCF $230, mid-cycle $260) is below my round-1 $296. Scenarios: bear $150 (25%), base $267 (50%), bull $342 (25%, lowered from $370 to an 18x multiple). The ladder is a three-lognormal mixture (sigmas 0.25/0.20/0.18) plus a 5% wide tail component: mean ~$263, median ~$262, P(up) ~61%, P(<$166) ~17%. The ladder sits slightly above the blended fair value because the FCF leg is a deliberately rate-harsh cross-check. Research limits: Kalshi returned 429 and Polymarket's December page was the 2025 market, so Fed odds rest on the Kalshi search snapshot and the DeFi Rate aggregator; the Moody's capex note returned 403. Peer forward EV/EBITDA is estimated from trailing figures and peer growth is 3-year CAGR.
