memo.title: NVDA: long a decade-low 19.5x NTM multiple; target $268.93, stop $174.61, add only if late-Oct capex guides clear our base case
memo.call_reason: Published 12-month target $268.93 is 12.6% above the $238.90 close, P(gain) is 0.63 and the conviction rubric reads medium, but the expected excess return barely covers ~38% volatility, so the position stays small and staged.
memo.one_liner: NVDA trades at ~19.5x NTM EPS, a decade low and below AVGO/TSM, with FY28 guided to ~+70% revenue; even after assuming the multiple compresses to 16x we get a $263 research target (12m) and a $268.93 target. The risk is a 2027-28 hyperscaler capex digestion, so we hold 1 share and add only if the Oct 27-30 capex guides and the ~Nov 17-18 Q3 FY27 print confirm demand.

thesis.point: The valuation already prices heavy de-rating: the stock is flat in a year only at ~13.9x Oct-2027 NTM EPS.
thesis.evidence: $238.90 is ~19.5x NTM consensus EPS of $12.00-12.25 (Q3 FY27-Q2 FY28; stockanalysis fwd P/E 19.34x), vs AVGO 20.49x and TSM 20.65x. Consistent Oct-2027 NTM EPS of $17.1 means a flat year needs ~13.9x, a further ~29% de-rating. All five agents assume compression to 16-17x and still reach research targets (12m) of $250-296.

thesis.point: Earnings visibility through FY28 is unusually high and supply-constrained.
thesis.evidence: Q2 FY27 revenue $96.2B (+106% y/y), Data Center $89.0B (+117%), non-GAAP GM 75.0%. The Q3 guide is $108.0B ±2% at 74.0% GM. Management's preliminary FY28 view is ~+70% revenue at 72-73% GM after a 71-72% Q4 trough. $279B of supply and capacity commitments back the ramp.

thesis.point: Customer capex keeps being revised up, and backlogs fund the 2027 ramp.
thesis.evidence: Big-4 2026 capex guides rose from ~$655B to $732.5B during the year, and none was cut. 2027 Big-4 consensus is $934.5B (IO Fund) to $1,029B (S&P), against our base case of $1,080B. Backlogs: MSFT commercial RPO $678B, Google Cloud $513.9B, AWS $496B. Year-ahead consensus drift was +25% to +62% in each of 2024-26.

memo.variant_view: There is no strong variant view against the options market. Our $268.93 target and 0.63 P(gain) sit close to the options-only distribution (target $263.75, P(gain) 0.61, 15th percentile $173.36). Against the sell side we are more cautious: the 50-analyst median target is $315 (range $210-515, Strong Buy), ~17% above ours. The gap is the multiple, not EPS: we assume 16x on Oct-2027 NTM EPS because FY29 growth should slow to low-to-mid teens. Our customer-capex work adds a second gap. At base capture, base-case 2027 capex implies FY28 revenue of ~$647B, 6% below the $687B consensus, and NVIDIA's supply cap (~$700-750B) limits FY28 upside. So we are below the Street on both multiple and FY28 revenue, and in line with options. [sources 9, 11, 12]

valuation.methods: Supervisor research target (12m) $263 is a blend of two legs. P/E (60%): consistent Oct-2027 NTM EPS (Q3 FY28-Q2 FY29) of $17.1 = H2 FY28 consensus $8.90 + H1 FY29 ~$8.5 (FY29 +13-15%, ~2% memory-cost haircut), x 16x = $274. FCF yield (40%): $17.1 x 23.9B shares x 72% conversion = $12.3/share at a 5.0% yield = $246, + ~$1 net cash = $247. Agent research targets (12m) $250/$255/$260/$270/$296 (median $260). agent_4 is high on 17x and a 4.5% yield. 16x is ~22% below the AVGO/TSM 20.57x anchor. The published target $268.93 is the median of the blended options-plus-agents distribution. Thesis break $160.

agents.method_text: Kilian's legs at the horizon: 0.4 x EV/EBITDA 11x NTM GAAP EBITDA $204B ($165) + 0.4 x SOTP with the compute fleet run off by vintage at spot ($60) + 0.2 x P/E 18x ($145) = $119.21 on 13,137M economic shares; 8.75 GW at YE27, ~$48/W-yr through 2027 fading to the ~$19 break-even by 2032, capex $38/W.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.inputs: 11.0x NTM (Q4-27 to Q3-28) GAAP EBITDA ~$204,138M (0.19 x FY27 $155,741M + 0.81 x FY28 $215,490M); less net debt at H $53,103M, EchoStar $8.5B and the expected Tesla transfer $18B, plus digital assets $1.6B; / 13,136.9M economic shares

inputs_detail.derivation: Class A 8,240M + Class B 5,339M outstanding at 2026-09-30 = 13,579M (incl. 389.3M Cursor merger shares, 8-K 2026-08-14) less 1,302M Musk performance-restricted Class B shares (1,000M vest only with market-cap tranches AND a permanent Mars colony of 1M people; 302.1M with tranches AND 100 TW of non-Earth compute; 424B4 "2026 Compensation Developments", vesting deemed improbable, no expense; Reuters reported the same awards pre-split as 200M and 60.4M) = 12,277M, plus ~533M dilutive awards (Q3 diluted 12,475M - basic 11,942M weighted). The company already leaves the restricted shares out of basic EPS (basic 11,942M vs 13,579M outstanding, Ex. 99.1).
inputs_detail.variant_view: Counting all 1,302M restricted shares (round-1 basis): fair value $109.02 (-8.6%).

inputs_detail.derivation: 12,810M + 261.8M EchoStar consideration shares (424B4; Spectrum Acquisition Closing assumed ~2027-11-30 per CORRESP, priced in by the horizon) + 65.1M expected restricted shares (5% chance the Mars / 100 TW award is re-cut to attainable terms, as xAI-era awards were reset) = 13,136.9M. tax_assumptions._future_note: Combined rate you'd expect on today's embedded gains when you'd otherwise sell (15% federal + ~6% state once working). Drives the sell cost and the gain-harvest suggestion.
tax_assumptions._tax_note: Kilian 2026-09-28: taxable account; ~$20,000 internship wages in 2026 plus realized gains; claimed as a dependent by a parent living in CA; full-time student under 24 living in CT. Assumed (not confirmed): domicile stays CA (a student living away at school keeps the parents' domicile, FTB Pub 1031), CT dorm is not a permanent place of abode so CT does not tax investment income; kiddie tax applies (earned income not more than half of his support). Federal 2026 figures from IRS Rev. Proc. 2025-32; CA brackets are 2025 (FTB Tax News Oct 2025), 2026's not published yet.
tax_assumptions._other_unearned_note: Dividends etc. this year (rough: GOOGL + META dividends). Counts toward the kiddie-tax threshold.
tax_assumptions._kiddie_note: Unearned income above $2,700 (2 x $1,350, Rev. Proc. 2025-32) is taxed at the parent's rate, federal (Form 8615) and CA (FTB 3800). Applies to a full-time student 19-23 whose earned income is not more than half of his own support.
tax_assumptions._parent_note: Kilian 2026-10-20 22:04Z: parent in NYC, 37% federal bracket. Parent's NY/NYC rates do not apply to Kilian's gains (no NY kiddie tax under Form 8615).
tax_assumptions._flat_note: Kilian 2026-10-20 22:04Z: the parent claiming him lives in New York City (37% federal bracket; NY 9.65%, NYC 3.876% at the parent's income). Federal kiddie tax (Form 8615): unearned income above kiddie_threshold ($2,700) at the parent's federal rates, short-term 37%, long-term 20% (the 37% bracket is above the 20% LTCG start, Rev. Proc. 2025-32); up to the threshold at Kilian's own federal rates, 10% short-term (wages $20k less the $16,100 dependent standard deduction leave ~$3.9k taxable, inside the 10% band to $12,400) and 0% long-term. New York has no kiddie tax when Form 8615 is used: the child's investment income is reported on the child's own NY return and taxed at the child's own rates (NYS IT-201-I, 'Does your child have investment income over $2,700?'). So NY and NYC tax every gain at Kilian's own marginal rates: NY 5.40% ($13,900-80,650) + NYC 3.762% ($12,000-25,000), single, 2026 schedules (NYS IT-2105-I 2026); NY dependent standard deduction $3,100. Assumed: Kilian is domiciled at the parent's NYC home (a dependent student keeps the parents' domicile) and his CT dorm is not a permanent place of abode. NIIT dropped (Kilian 2026-10-21 00:48Z 'yes you may drop it'; it was kept per his 2026-10-01 20:32Z ask): Form 8960 applies it on the child's own MAGI over $200,000 (single), which his income does not reach. Short-term = 37% + 9.162% = 46.162%; long-term = 20% + 9.162% = 29.162%; own rates under the threshold 19.162% / 9.162%. Was CA (41.3% / 28.1% / 14% / 2%) until 2026-10-20. Net losses offset gains; up to $3,000 deducts at the own short-term rate. Bracket mode (mode 'brackets') still holds the CA schedule and is not updated.
tax_assumptions._short_term_all_note: Kilian 2026-10-28 card 'Assume short-term on all' (thread 'Fix AMAT target vs sell mismatch'): every holding is assumed sold within the year at the short-term rate, so a trim only pays the same tax H years sooner; band per year = q tau (1 - (1+d)^-H) / H + spread / T. Overrides lot_aware_horizon; false restores it.
tax_assumptions._lot_aware_note: Kilian 2026-10-20 card 'Lot-aware' (Assumption audit thread): a short-term lot's trim band compares selling now with holding it to its one-year date and selling long-term: band per year = q (tau_now - flat_long_term_rate (1+d)^-X) / X, X = years until the oldest (FIFO) lot turns long-term (floor 1 day), plus spread / T. Long-term lots keep the T-year rule (years_until_you_would_otherwise_sell, future_rate_on_deferred_gains, Claude defaults 2026-09-28). false restores the T-year rule for every lot.

agents.reasoning: Round 2 (supervisor fact-checks plus a direct read of the AT&T Q3 call transcript, 10-Q R63/R17 and FCC auction notes). Evidence: Q3 2026 revenue $32.3B (+5.3%), adj. EBITDA $12.5B (+5.4%), adj. EPS $0.65, FCF ~$5.0B; 379k postpaid phone adds, churn 0.92%; postpaid phone ARPU +4% from new/refreshed plans and back-book pricing with promotions unchanged (call); fiber ARPU -4% with Q4 similar and "relatively stable ARPU" over 2026-28 (CFO). GAAP EPS $0.12-0.13 carries a $2.6B Mexico impairment and an ~$800M separation charge whose cash lands mainly in 2027. Guides: 2026 EPS ~$2.40, AC EBITDA mid-to-high single digits, consolidated EBITDA 5%+ in 2028, FCF $18B+/$19B+/$21B+, capital investment $22-23B in 2027-28, $24B+ buybacks, 2.5x leverage in 2029. Price moves: Oct 9 (-10.8%) = SpaceX buying Grain's 800 MHz licences (no ex-dividend effect: ex-date Oct 12); Oct 21 (-6.4%) = results day (phone-add miss, capex/working-capital framing), a small earnings-path change; Oct 23 (-8.0%) = Bloomberg report of SpaceX seeking 80,000+ sites, a multiple effect. What changed from round 1: Forged Fiber stake $4,058M x 0.9 (R63) instead of $2.58B; separation cash no longer double-counted in net debt (horizon $147.9B, now linked to driver FCF); wireless ARPU +1.5%/+0.8% (was +0.6%/+0.4%); fiber ARPU -1.0%/+0.5% (was +0.7%/+1.6%); AC EBITDA +6.0%/+6.0%; interest +$0.1B; upper C-band -$5B x 0.35; P/E 8.1x and FCF yield 12.3% held at today's levels (were 8.5x / 12.0%); EPS, FCF/share and horizon net debt are now computed from the drivers through driver_build.set. Peers: Kilian's 12 incumbents on CY2027E, after leases: EV/EBITDA median 5.52x (5.98x ex-DT), P/E 10.55x; AT&T 5.78x / 7.98x on that basis. Result: research target (12m) $23.88 (EV/EBITDA $23.43, P/E $24.37, FCF $24.26); bear $15.15 (price war, 5.3x), bull $29.23 (6.9x). Guidance record: EPS first guides met or beaten 3 of 3 (median +2.7%), FCF floors 3 of 3 (+3.75%); we sit just below the 2027 FCF floor ($18.9B) and the 2028 EBITDA 5% (4.7% ex-Mexico) because of Legacy and fiber ARPU, and above the 2028 EPS floor on buybacks. Ladder: 60% the scenario mixture (lognormal, 15% within-scenario vol), 40% a neutral 28%-vol distribution centred near spot, because the October de-rating came from SpaceX headlines that may continue and momentum is negative; median ~$22.8, P(>= $21) 0.605. All value legs are driver-linked; the dividend and peer-median cross-checks carry zero weight.

supervisor.summary: AT&T's research target (12m) is $22.99, the engine value of a driver set rebuilt from evidence on 2026-11-10 and corrected in the citation-gate fix (was $23.15 before the rebuild). The two biggest finds: the retiree health plan's prior-service credit, which props up adjusted EPS, mostly runs out in 2027 (10-K Note 14 balance; other income ~2,290 in 2026 -> ~1,189 in 2027 and ~551 after), and SpaceX's mobile entry now takes about 0.44M / 0.67M of AT&T's 2028-29 phone adds on top of the post-SpaceX 6.1x multiple Kilian kept. Revenue per phone is built from price actions (flat without one, a half-size back-book rise in 2028), Internet Air adds fade, home internet ARPU -2% in 2027, and AC EBITDA follows a 0.84 flow-through on service revenue from a Q4 2026 base of 11,696. The result sits moderately below management and consensus: 2028 adjusted EPS $2.78 vs the $2.82 floor, FCF $17.6B / $19.8B vs $19B+ / $21B+, consolidated EBITDA 3.0% under consensus in 2028 (50,995 vs 52,561). One card is open for Kilian (management's 20%+ home internet revenue pace, +7.8%), plus two smaller option sets (industry phone pool after 2026, home internet quarter shape).

memo.title: AT&T (T) Long: SpaceX de-rating priced in, cash path intact - target $22.65, research target (12m) $23.16 plus a 5.3% yield
memo.call_reason: The published target ($22.65) is above the $20.93 price and conviction is medium (rubric), with a 5.3% dividend on top and a stop at $16.54 that sits on the $16.5 thesis-break level.
memo.one_liner: AT&T lost ~16% in October on SpaceX headlines (Grain 800 MHz licences, a reported 80,000-site push) while Q3 beat and 2026 EPS was raised; our horizon multiples keep that de-rating and still value the shares at a research target (12m) of $23.16 (+10.6%) on the earnings path alone. We buy 167 shares at or below the page's Entry below (~$21.60), ahead of this week's peer prints and the Oct-29 FCC vote, stop $16.54, take-profit $27.52.

thesis.point: Earnings power is rising, not falling: EPS growth from lower D&A and ~5% a year of buybacks carries value even at today's de-rated multiples.
thesis.evidence: Q3 2026 revenue $32.3B (+5.3%), adjusted EBITDA $12.5B (+5.4%), adjusted EPS $0.65; 2026 EPS guide raised to ~$2.40, mainly on lower depreciation from held-for-sale accounting for Mexico. Our driver build gives adjusted EPS $2.66 (2027) and $2.91 (2028) vs Zacks consensus $2.54 / $2.86; at 8.3x (AT&T's own NTM P/E today) the P/E leg alone is $24.01.

thesis.point: The October drawdown is a multiple event, and we keep it in the target rather than betting on a rebound.
thesis.evidence: Closes fell 24.87 -> 22.18 (-10.8%) on Oct-9 (SpaceX buys Grain's 800 MHz licences), 23.42 -> 21.91 (-6.4%) on results day Oct-21, and 22.74 -> 20.93 (-8.0%) on Oct-23 (Bloomberg: SpaceX seeks 80,000+ sites). The horizon EV/EBITDA stays at the post-news 6.1x (~$2.8/sh of de-rating retained; 6.1x = 5.69x on the peer basis vs an 11-incumbent median of 5.98x ex-DT). SpaceX targets next-generation service by end-2027, so most fourth-carrier cash-flow damage falls after our 2027-10-23 horizon.

thesis.point: Cash returns and asset sales put a floor under the equity.
thesis.evidence: $0.2775 quarterly dividend (5.3% yield at $20.93), $24B+ of buybacks guided for 2026-28, Mexico sale for ~$2.0B cash at closing (Q1 2027) and a 50% fiber JV stake carried at $4,058M (taken at x0.9 = +$3.65B). At the $16.5 thesis break the stock would yield 6.7% and ~15% FCF-to-common at ~5.2x EBITDA on the peer basis, a level consistent only with a broken cash path.

memo.variant_view: We sit between the Street and the options market. Sell-side (24 analysts, Buy) has a median target of $28.00 (mean $27.80, range $20-34), roughly 21% above our research target (12m) of $23.16: we keep the post-SpaceX 6.1x EV/EBITDA and model FCF of $18.5B / $19.9B for 2027-28, below both management's $19B+ / $21B+ floors and consensus ($19.24B / $20.97B), because Legacy EBITDA turns negative after 2027 and wireless ARPU growth fades to +0.75% in 2028. The options market is more bearish than we are: its standalone 12-month median is $21.35 with P(gain) 52.7%, vs our published 60.2%. Our variant view is therefore narrow and specific: EPS (above consensus on lower D&A and buybacks) carries value at a de-rated multiple, so we do not need the SpaceX fear to fade to make money; a move back toward the pre-October ~6.8x would add ~$2.8/sh on top. This is not a large mispricing call; most of the expected return is the dividend plus a modest earnings-path gain.

valuation.methods: Research target (12m) $23.16 = model-engine base horizon value (23.1576) of the supervisor's reconciled driver set (wireless and fiber subs x ARPU, Advanced Connectivity margin, capital investment ~$23.4B/22.8B/22.7B): EV/EBITDA 6.1x on NTM EBITDA ~$50.4B = $22.55 (weight 0.5), P/E 8.3x on driver-linked NTM EPS $2.86 = $24.01 (0.35), 12.3% FCF yield on $2.82/share = $23.19 (0.15); net debt at horizon $144.3B, NCI $18.0B, preferred $2.95B, fiber stake +$3.65B, expected upper C-band spend -$2.0B (-$5B x 0.4), 6,387M shares. No DCF leg (not in the DCF policy for this sector). The five forecasters' values span $22.24-24.39. The published target $22.65 is the median of the final distribution, which blends the options market (weight 0.67, median $21.35) with the research ladder (0.33); expected value $23.42 (+11.9%), P(gain) 60.2%. Bear values $15.15-16.68 (price war, cable-like ~5.2-5.3x), bull values $27.51-29.23 (re-rating toward ~6.8-7.0x).

risks.risk: SpaceX becomes a priced, national fourth carrier (Grain 800 MHz + EchoStar spectrum + leased terrestrial sites); supervisor probability 0.35 over 2028-2031, and the market can price it well before then (bear values $15.15-16.68).
risks.signpost: A signed site-lease deal for tens of thousands of towers; FCC approval of the Grain licences with terrestrial rights; a US price list for Starlink Mobile; Polymarket odds of a US carrier by end-2027 rising from 34.5% (thin market).

risks.risk: Free cash flow misses the floors and buybacks slow: we already sit below management ($18.5B vs $19B+ in 2027), and the 2025 tax-law cash benefit runs off after 2027.
risks.signpost: Q4 print guides 2027 FCF below $19B or capital investment above $23B; buyback pace below the ~$24B+ 2026-28 plan.

risks.risk: Wireless price competition: Verizon is taking share (406k Q3 phone adds, guide raised to 1.1-1.2M) while AT&T adds slowed to 379k; fiber ARPU is already -4% y/y.
risks.signpost: AT&T postpaid phone adds below ~300k a quarter, churn above 1.0%, postpaid phone ARPU growth falling from +4% toward +1%, rising promotions on the Q4 call.

risks.risk: Balance sheet: 3.13x leverage with the 2.5x target pushed to 2029, a Fitch BBB+ Negative Outlook, $9.5B of debt due within a year and possible ~$5B upper C-band spend.
risks.signpost: A Fitch downgrade, AT&T qualifying to bid heavily in Auction 115, refinancing at materially higher coupons.

what_changes_our_mind: A signed SpaceX terrestrial site deal at national scale (tens of thousands of towers) or FCC approval of the Grain licences with full terrestrial flexibility before mid-2027: move to No position.
The late-January Q4 print guides 2027 FCF below $19B, slows the $24B+ buyback plan, or shows postpaid phone adds below ~300k with ARPU growth fading: exit.

Upside case: SpaceX talks end in a wholesale/partner deal with incumbents and AT&T holds +4% phone ARPU with adds back above 400k; the multiple can revert toward ~6.8x (~+$2.8/sh), so we would hold through the take-profit review rather than trim.

FY27 adjusted EPS ~$17.75 sits at the Street ($17.71, Nasdaq/Zacks); the stock trades at ~23.9x NTM vs an 18.45x six-peer median (five US peers on Zacks consensus EPS, Daikin a derived NTM estimate of unverified EPS basis), and the exit keeps only the rule-based premium (22.7x). No judgment call moves the target more than 5%.

agents.reasoning: Round 2. Filings first: Q3'26 revenue $6,760M (+18%), bookings $7,248M, backlog $12.5B (+73%), EMEA/APAC margins down, FY EPS guide only reaffirmed; the call put Q4 adjusted EPS at $3.40-3.50 (incl. 10c tax) vs a $3.59 Street, cut FY price to ~1pt and FY organic leverage to 'low 20s' (from 25%+) - why the beat sold off 8.6%. >$8B of the $12.5B backlog is for 2027+ and >$1B for 2028, so FY27 Americas +11% is largely booked. Supervisor findings acted on: (1) peer median rebuilt on 6 whole-company peers (CSW dropped): 18.3x on the peers.md figures (supervisor 18.45x on Nasdaq quarterly peer EPS); own NTM 23.93x on post-print consensus; exit 22.7x, no -0.5 turn (it double counted the k=0.8 shrink on a market-priced multiple). (2) Net debt now includes supplier finance $393.1M (10-Q, in accounts payable): 3,383.3. (3) NCI at market (-488: 9M NCI earnings $20.0M annualised x 18.3x) and the asbestos plan balance (-275 = $545M plan - $270M QSF, 10-K) as adjustments; the supervisor's extra -197.5 x 0.4 court estimate is not in the 10-K and is left out. (4) SBC counted once: share count -1.8%/yr on gross buybacks. (5) EV/EBITDA cross-check on whole-company filers only: 14.1x median, exit 19.0x. (6) JCI's print was Oct 27, outside the 1-month window. Where I disagree: the supervisor says 'Q4 incrementals north of 25%' is not in the transcript; the TradingKey transcript (source 4) has the CEO saying 'our incremental leverage in the fourth quarter, we're projecting to be north of our target range' (target 25%+) - I re-cite it to source 4 and keep it, while taking the FY 'low 20s' cut into the Americas path (+30bp FY27, ~23.8% reported incrementals). Tax 18.5% FY26 / 19.5% FY27-28 (was 20%). Model FY27 GAAP EPS $17.83 vs Street $17.71 and whisper $18.10 (adjusted ~$18.1). Guidance record: every first annual EPS guide FY23-26 beaten (median +5.8%); FY26 incremental target missed. The net effect of the fixes is small (443.6 -> 442.9): removing the haircut, the lower tax and the share count lift the P/E leg, supplier finance/NCI/asbestos and the lower EV/EBITDA multiple take it back. Downside (P10) = data-center order pause + margin -200bp + de-rate to the peer median; upside (P90) = faster burn, 25%+ incrementals, multiple held. sec.gov refuses scripted access without a contact email, so filings were read with WebFetch. All legs driver-linked; no custom legs.

agents.method_text: Blend of 9.5x NTM adjusted (pre-SBC) EBITDA at the horizon ($8.41B, after Cogentrix and the Meta PPAs) = $171.0 (70%) and a DCF at 9.15% WACC with 2.0% Gordon growth = $140.9 (30%). Equals the standard engine's base horizon value of $161.96.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.inputs: NTM adj. EBITDA at horizon $8,414M x 9.5x = EV $79.9B - net debt $20.9B - preferred/NCI $2.49B + Cogentrix tax NPV $0.63B = $57.2B / 334.3M shares (incl. ~1.1M SBC shares) = $171.0

inputs_detail.derivation: Estimate derived from reported 10-Q lines at 2026-06-30 (no net-debt figure is reported): long-term debt due currently 1,876 + long-term debt less current 17,719 = 19,595, less cash and cash equivalents 435 = 19,160. Excludes AR financing 300, the forward repurchase obligation 613 and restricted cash 46. [citation gate 2026-10-14]

Estimate: sum of two reported XBRL facts at 2026-06-30 (10-Q accn 0001692819-26-000019): PreferredStockValue 2,476 + MinorityInterest 12 = 2,488. Treated as debt-like claims ahead of common equity. [citation gate 2026-10-14]

19,160 + Cogentrix cash 2,300 and assumed debt 1,500 (src 5) - ~15 months of Adj. FCFbG at ~4,300/yr = ~5,400 (2026 guidance midpoint, src 3) + growth spend ex-Cogentrix ~1,500 (part of the $4.5-5B 2026-27 growth allocation, src 4) + buybacks ~1,250 (remaining ~$1.2B authorization by YE2027, src 3) + common and preferred dividends ~580 = ~20,900. The $1.5B junior subordinated notes (src 9) raise debt and cash equally, so they are left out of the net figure. The notes' prospectus says proceeds may redeem the 8.0% Series A and 7.0% Series B preferred after their Oct/Dec 2026 resets (src 25); if so, ~$1.5B shifts from preferred to net debt and total claims ahead of common (~$23.4B) are unchanged, so the bridge keeps that total.

335.6M outstanding (2026-08-03, F103) - ~7.4M repurchased with ~$1.15B at ~$155 (remaining authorization, src 3) + 5.0M Cogentrix consideration shares (src 5) + ~1.1M stock-comp shares (SBC dilution: TTM SBC $134M (F46) / ~$150 x 1.25 years) = 335.6 - 7.42 + 5.0 + 1.12 = ~334.3M (corrected from 334.6M, an addition error, citation gate 2026-10-14). SBC is counted here, not in FCFF.

inputs_detail.input: NTM adjusted EBITDA at horizon (Q4-2027 to Q3-2028)
inputs_detail.derivation: Model rows: FY2027 8,104 (= low end of the $7.4-7.8B 2027 midpoint opportunity, which management said is trending to the lower end, src 4, plus ~$700M from Cogentrix (~$4.0B / 7.25x = ~$550M, Vistra release src 6) and the Meta PPA premium (src 4, 7)); FY2028 8,497 (+~5%: full Meta operating delivery by YE2027 (src 7), PJM capacity flat at $325 vs $333 (src 8), ERCOT soft, only ~72% hedged (src 3)). NTM = 0.21 x FY2027 + 0.79 x FY2028. Pre-SBC, the same basis as peer consensus adjusted EBITDA (src 27). The thin FMP consensus for the window (~$9,370M, 1-4 analysts, src 19) is not used; this sits ~10% below it.

Peer NTM EV/EBITDA median 10.6x, range 8.9x (NRG) to 11.8x (CEG), on consensus adjusted (pre-SBC) EBITDA (src 20, 27). VST trades ~9.5-9.8x today: EV ~$72.7B (152.2 x 335.6M = $51.1B + $19.16B net debt + $2.49B preferred/NCI) on ~$7.4-7.6B NTM EBITDA before the deals. 9.5x is about where it trades now, ~1.1x below the median, between NRG and TLN. The discount reflects merchant ERCOT exposure (2028 only ~72% hedged, src 3), the undecided PJM 2030/31+ design with a consumer push to cap existing generation (src 23, 24), and the gas-heavy fleet vs CEG. No premium is claimed.
$700M = '~$0.7 billion of net present value of expected tax benefits' in Vistra's release (src 6) x 0.9 closing probability = $630M (~$1.9/share).

methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: FY2026-29 FCFF (adj. EBITDA ~37% of revenue, capex 14%->9.5%, 20% tax, SBC as dilution not cost) discounted at 9.15%; Gordon terminal growth 2.0% after FY2029 (~86% of DCF value); exit-9.0x cross-check $153

inputs_detail.derivation: FY2025 revenue 17,586 (F3); TTM to 2026-06-30 18,985 (F6) supports ~19,600 for FY2026; FY2027 adds Cogentrix's 5,500 MW (src 5,6) and Meta deliveries; later years grow with load at 3-4%.
Capex FY2025 2,752 (F57), TTM 2,866 (F60, ~15% of TTM revenue, includes growth projects); declines as the Permian peakers and other growth projects are completed.

FY2025 SBC 113 / revenue 17,586 = 0.64% (F43, F3); TTM 134 (F46) on ~19,600 FY2026 revenue = ~0.7%. Under sbc_treatment 'dilution' it is carried as ~1.1M extra shares by the horizon instead of a cash cost.

Cost of equity 10.71% = 10-yr UST 5.21% on 2026-10-13 (src 21) + beta ~1.1 (judgment for a merchant IPP) x 5% ERP. Pre-tax marginal debt cost 6.5%: TTM average 5.8% (interest 1,132 / debt 19,595, F81/F98) is below today's marginal cost, shown by the 7.000%/7.250% junior notes issued 2026-09-24 (src 9); x (1 - 20%) = 5.2%. Preferred ~7.5% (8.0%/7.0% series, src 25). Weights on EV $72.7B: 70.3% equity, 26.4% net debt, 3.4% preferred -> 9.16%, used as 9.15% (round 1: 8.5% with 5.24% rf and 5.8% debt cost).

inputs_detail.input: Terminal value: Gordon growth after FY2029
inputs_detail.derivation: Nominal FCFF growth of 2.0% after FY2029, below long-run inflation of ~2.5%, to price post-horizon risks: PJM's 2030/31+ design is undecided (src 23) with a consumer proposal to keep the cap on existing generation (src 24); ERCOT oversupply as 2028+ hedges roll off (src 3); AI capex low case (src 26). Cross-check: the round-1 9.0x exit on FY2029 EBITDA gives a DCF of $153 at 9.15%, which is equivalent to ~2.35% perpetual growth; I prefer the Gordon form so the DCF does not reuse peer multiples.

thesis.evidence: CFO on the Q2 call: 2027 'trending towards the lower end' and Cogentrix plus Meta 'add roughly $700 million'; hedges 100%/94%/72% for 2026/27/28. EIA's September STEO held 2027 ERCOT generation at ~527 TWh and raised 2027 ERCOT North to $34.30/MWh, so the August load-growth cut did not extend.

thesis.point: At ~$138 the stock trades at ~9x forward EBITDA, only ~1.8 turns above the 7.25x plain gas-fleet M&A mark, so the contracted nuclear (Meta 2.6 GW PJM, AWS 1.2 GW Comanche Peak) and PJM capacity at the $325 cap are cheaply valued.
thesis.evidence: Cogentrix bought at 7.25x 2027 EBITDA; PJM 2028/29 BRA cleared at the $325/MW-day cap (10,924 MW for Vistra) and the collar extends through 2029/30; ~$23.5B net debt plus preferred and ~337M diluted shares give ~$105 at 7.2x.

thesis.point: Insiders and the balance sheet are supportive: the CEO bought in the open market after the drawdown, and the preferred is being refinanced into cheaper junior notes rather than equity.
thesis.evidence: CEO Form 4 purchases Aug 24 and Aug 31-Sep 1, 2026; $1.5B 7.000%/7.250% junior subordinated notes (Sep 24) fund redemption of the 8.0% Series A and 7.0% Series B preferred at their resets. Offset: the CFO sold 20,000 shares at $151.03 under a 10b5-1 plan.

memo.variant_view: Versus the Street we are the bear: our $150.54 target is ~31% below the weighted analyst median of $218.97 (17 analysts, low $169 Mizuho, high $298). Street targets need ~11x EBITDA or ~$8.5B+ 2028 EBITDA, which requires ERCOT forwards to turn and new hyperscaler deals; with ~28% of 2028 unhedged into a curve still falling in late September, we don't underwrite that. Versus the options market we are only modestly more constructive: the market-implied median is $141.57 with P(gain) 0.52, against our $150.54 and 0.57; our edge is the belief that the Q3 guide formalizes ~$8.1B and that the EIA Texas load cut is already in the price. That is a small variant view, not a big one, and it is why the position is small.

valuation.methods: Supervisor blend, same as the five agents' mean ($150.9; range $145-156): (1) 9.0x ~$8.15B forward EBITDA = ~$73.4B EV, less ~$23.5B net debt plus preferred, over 337M diluted shares = ~$148 (50% weight); (2) ~$13.9/share FCF before growth at a 9% yield = ~$154 (30%); (3) ~13.5x ~$11.1 forward EPS = ~$150 (20%). Blend ~$151. The published 12-month target ($150.54) is the median of the combined options-market and agent distribution; expected value is $170.65 because of the fat right tail (q75 $206.50). Each 0.25x on the multiple is ~$6/share; the $8.1B vs $8.25B EBITDA dispute is ~$2.7/share.

catalysts.event: PJM Reliability Backstop Procurement bid window (~6.8 GW shortfall, cost cap $555/MW-day)
catalysts.why_it_moves: Clearing prices near the cap would confirm scarcity value in PJM and data-center-paid capacity; a weak outcome or political cost-allocation fights would pressure the PJM story ahead of the BRA.
catalysts.watch: Procured MW vs the 6,831 MW target and the clearing price relative to $325 and $555/MW-day.

catalysts.event: Series A preferred first reset / earliest redemption date (8.0% rate ends); Series B reset in Dec 2026
catalysts.why_it_moves: Redemption funded by the Sep-24 junior notes removes the reset risk and lowers the fixed charge; mostly housekeeping.
catalysts.watch: Redemption notice/8-K for the full $1.0B Series A; no equity issuance.

catalysts.event: FOMC rate decision
catalysts.why_it_moves: IPP multiples compressed as the 10-year approached 5%; VST is a levered, high-multiple name, so a hawkish surprise hits it harder than the market.
catalysts.watch: Hike vs hold and the 10-year's reaction; a move back above 5% is a multiple headwind.

catalysts.event: Q3 2026 earnings and formal 2026/2027 guidance update including Cogentrix and Meta
catalysts.why_it_moves: This is the event that formalizes (or breaks) the ~$8.1B 2027 base the whole valuation sits on, and gives the first read on 2028 hedging.
catalysts.watch: 2027 guide at or above ~$8.1B incl. ~$0.7B Cogentrix+Meta (below $7.4B low end is a thesis hit); 2028 hedge % and price; buyback pace; any new hyperscaler contract; whether guidance waits for the Cogentrix close.

catalysts.event: Cogentrix acquisition close (FERC approved Aug 2026; HSR and customary conditions outstanding)
catalysts.why_it_moves: Unlocks ~5.5 GW of gas and the Cogentrix share of the $0.7B EBITDA add; a slip delays the formal 2027 guide.
catalysts.watch: Closing 8-K; 5M shares issued to seller; $1.5B assumed debt.

catalysts.event: ERCOT files the Batch Zero Eligibility Verification and Community Impact Review reports (governor-ordered data-center audit); energization of new 75 MW+ loads paused until then
catalysts.why_it_moves: Determines how much of the Texas large-load queue is real, which drives the ERCOT load-growth narrative and the 2028 forward curve on VST's open volume.
catalysts.watch: Share of the ~128 GW studied load that survives; restart date for Batch Zero and energizations; any new PUCT rules for large loads or co-location.

catalysts.date: mid-Dec 2026 (agents cite 2026-12-15 close; PJM confirms December)
catalysts.event: PJM 2029/2030 Base Residual Auction under the $325 cap / $175 floor collar
catalysts.why_it_moves: Sets East capacity revenue for June 2029 onward; a fourth cap-level clear supports the out-year story (adds nothing to NTM EBITDA).
catalysts.watch: Clearing price vs $325 cap; reserve shortfall; any talk of extending the collar or more affordability intervention.

catalysts.event: Texas 90th Legislature convenes (session through late May 2027)
catalysts.why_it_moves: Bills on large-load limits, data-center cost allocation or co-location could cut the ERCOT demand story that underpins 2028+ pricing.
catalysts.watch: Filed bills on large-load interconnection, curtailment or co-location; committee hearings in Feb-Mar.

catalysts.event: Q4 2026 results: first 2028 outlook and updated hedge levels (~72% hedged as of Aug 2026)
catalysts.why_it_moves: The 2028 view tells us whether EBITDA grows past 2027 or rolls over as the open ~28% re-hedges at weaker ERCOT forwards; it sets the NTM base at our horizon.
catalysts.watch: 2028 opportunity range vs ~$8.1-8.2B; hedge % and realized prices; buyback authorization.

risks.risk: The Q3 guide lands below the $7.4B low end plus $0.7B, or the 2028 view comes in below 2027, as the ~28% open 2028 volume is re-hedged into weak ERCOT forwards.
risks.signpost: ERCOT 2027/2028 forwards keep falling week over week (they were down ~2.0%/1.7% in the week of Sep 21); management language shifts from 'lower end' to 'below the range'; continued downward EPS revisions.

risks.risk: Texas large-load demand disappoints: the Dec 10 audit culls much of the queue and the 2027 legislature restricts data-center interconnection, cementing the ~$30-34/MWh ERCOT curve.
risks.signpost: Audit reports show a large share of the 128 GW studied load ineligible; Batch Zero restart pushed to late 2027; another EIA STEO cut to Texas load growth (August already cut 2027 to 6% from 14%).

risks.risk: Sector de-rating: IPPs trade as a group on AI-power sentiment and rates; a hyperscaler capex pause or a 10-year above 5% compresses the multiple toward the 7.25x gas-fleet mark (~$105).
risks.signpost: CEG/NRG/TLN falling together with VST; hyperscaler capex guidance cuts; 10-year sustained above 5%.

risks.risk: PJM political intervention: extended or tighter price caps, data-center cost allocation or backstop design that caps East capacity value.
risks.signpost: White House/governor pressure for lower caps, a FERC order changing the collar beyond 2029/30, or the backstop procurement clearing far below cap.

trade.position: 5 sh (~$690, 6.9% of the $10,000 book); binding limit is the supervisor's 7% cap for overlap with the AI-power driver in META/GOOGL
trade.entry: Staged per the supervisor: buy ~3 sh now at ~$138, add the last ~2 sh after the Q3 call (calendars: Nov 5) only if the 2027 guide is at or above ~$8.1B incl. Cogentrix and Meta; hold the second tranche if the guide is below the $7.4B low end or Cogentrix has not closed.
trade.exit_or_add: Exit on a close below $104.94 (the ~$105 thesis break, ~7.2x EBITDA = gas-fleet M&A mark) or on a 2027 guide below $7.4B + $0.7B. Take profit at $206.50 (q75; ~11x, where the Street already is). Add the second tranche on a clean Q3 guide; consider going above the cap only with a new hyperscaler contract or a Dec 10 audit that clears most Batch Zero load. Expected loss at stop ~$165.

what_changes_our_mind: Q3 call guides 2027 below ~$7.9B including Cogentrix and Meta, or signals 2028 below 2027 (bearish: exit).
ERCOT 2028 forwards fall another ~10% into year-end or the Dec 10 audit/2027 legislature materially restricts large loads (bearish: cut).
A new hyperscaler contract (Comanche Peak expansion or a gas-backed PPA) plus a clean audit that reopens Batch Zero (bullish: lift target toward the Street and add above 7%).

invested_cash.meaning: dollar gain on stocks (price, dividends, realized and unrealized) / average dollars in stocks; SPY and equal weight = the same dollars on the same days in them instead

live_book.spy_basis: price plus distributions reinvested on the ex-date (dividends.json); no adjusted closes in the data
live_book.dividends_missing_note: names not in dividends.json are treated as paying nothing
live_book.note: 35 trading days of returns cannot show skill: daily stock returns swing by about 1-2%, so a gap of a few percent over a few weeks is well within luck. rough_se treats days as independent; read the gaps as what happened, not as evidence, until there are many months. Whole book: time-weighted, cash at the T-bill, vs fully invested SPY and equal weight. Invested cash: dollar-weighted on the stock sleeve, vs the same dollars in SPY and equal weight.
